Establish and uphold standards for data modeling, naming, metadata, integration and data sharing

Data Development and Operations

Lead the design, development and operation of ETL processes and data pipelines
Ensure recurring data production is accurate, timely and reconciled to authoritative sources, within published service levels
Monitor data flows, resolve issues promptly and drive root-cause remediation
Embed data quality checks, validation and controls throughout the data lifecycle
Ensure data is handled securely and protected from loss or unauthorized access, in line with legal and company standards

Modernization and Innovation

Continuously evaluate and adopt technologies, tools and practices that improve the scalability, efficiency and resilience of the data ecosystem
Partner with Technology on platform strategy, infrastructure and the path to production
Prepare and structure data to support advanced analytics and AI use cases

Data Enablement and Partnership

Manage the intake and prioritization of data requests transparently, with clear service levels
Promote data literacy and self-service through documentation, data dictionaries and a community of practice
Serve as a trusted partner to business, analytics, AI and Technology teams on data definitions, changes and their downstream impacts
Partner with Data Governance to meet data quality, metadata, lineage and data risk requirements

Business-Managed Applications

Oversee a portfolio of business-managed applications that support key business processes, from intake and design through delivery, enhancement and ongoing support
Ensure these applications are well controlled and supported, and aligned to BMO technology, data and risk standards

People Leadership

Build, develop and lead a high-performing team of data professionals, working effectively with vendor partners
Set clear goals and accountability, coach for growth, and foster a culture of ownership, quality and continuous improvement
Attract, retain and develop top talent, recognizing strong performance and addressing gaps
Role model BMO values and foster an inclusive culture connected to our purpose
Take measured risks while protecting the bank by applying our Risk Management Framework in the execution of your role, in line with our Risk Culture and within our approved Risk Appetite, making sound and risk informed decisions that align to business strategy, protect assets, and adhere to applicable policy documents (Frameworks, Policies, Standards, Procedures and Supporting documents), laws and regulations.

Who You Are

Treats data as a product: curated, documented, reconciled and reusable
Holds a high standard for accuracy and builds processes that make quality repeatable
Balances stability with progress, modernizing while keeping production dependable
Understands Commercial Banking and how data flows across clients, products and channels
Communicates clearly and builds trust through transparency
Influences without authority and aligns diverse stakeholders around shared definitions
Thrives in ambiguity and brings creative solutions to complex, interdependent problems

Qualifications

9+ years of experience in data management, data engineering or a related field, including leadership of data teams
Deep expertise in ETL and data pipeline development, data modeling and data quality management
Strong proficiency in SQL and modern data programming languages such as Python
Experience with cloud and modern data platforms
Working knowledge of master data, metadata, semantic layer and data governance practices, including data privacy and integrity
Experience operating in a highly regulated environment; Commercial Banking or financial services experience is an asset
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills
Post-secondary degree in a related field of study, or an equivalent combination of education and experience

Why This Role

Lead the Data Foundation that underpins reporting, analytics and AI across Commercial Banking
Shape how data is built, managed and used at scale

Join a culture that values ownership, collaboration, trust and measurable outcomes

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
About Vitacore Industries

Vitacore was established on the conviction that Canada should have the domestic capability to produce critical healthcare products. The company became the first Canadian manufacturer of N95 respirators authorized by Health Canada, manufacturing locally in Burnaby from raw materials. Today, Vitacore generates approximately $10 million in revenue, with a product portfolio that includes surgical masks, respirators, related PPE, and Planet Impact, its program focused on recycling hard-to-recycle materials.

Vitacore is a founder-led organization characterized by speed, entrepreneurial judgment, and a disciplined appetite for growth. Mikhail Moore has built the company by identifying opportunities early and moving decisively. As the business enters its next phase, it requires a senior finance leader who can bring greater financial discipline, strategic insight, and scalable infrastructure while preserving the pace and commercial agility that have defined its success.

Download Full Job Description: Vitacore CFO - Position Profile.pdf

THE OPPORTUNITY

This is Vitacore’s first Chief Financial Officer appointment and a critical executive leadership role for the company’s next stage of scale. Reporting directly to the President, the CFO will serve as a strategic partner to ownership and leadership, establishing the financial architecture, governance discipline, capital strategy, and performance management framework required to support sustained growth. Priorities may include new markets, product expansion, strategic partnerships, government and institutional contracts, and potential external capital.

The role requires a CFO-calibre finance executive who can operate as both strategist and operator in a growing, founder-led business. The successful candidate will bring executive presence, commercial judgment, capital markets fluency, and the ability to influence enterprise decisions with confidence and credibility. Their mandate will extend beyond finance operations to include value creation, risk management, governance, capital allocation, and long-term enterprise planning.

FIRST-YEAR PRIORITIES

Required

Within the first year, the CFO will be expected to establish the financial leadership platform required for Vitacore’s next stage of growth, with measurable progress against the following priorities:

Implement a monthly close and reporting cadence that delivers accurate financial statements and executive reporting within an agreed timeline each month.
Develop a rolling 13-week cash flow forecast and 12-month financial outlook that provide clear visibility into liquidity, working capital, and capital requirements.
Establish a reliable product costing model and margin reporting framework covering key product lines, raw materials, labour, overhead, yield, and inventory movements.
Create an executive KPI dashboard that tracks revenue, gross margin, cash conversion, inventory turns, working capital, production efficiency, and capacity utilization.
Complete an assessment of accounting systems, ERP capability, internal controls, and finance team capacity, and present a prioritized roadmap for scalable infrastructure.
Prepare the company for future financing or strategic capital conversations by developing an investment narrative, integrated financial model, lender/investor materials, and data room readiness plan.
Build a practical finance team structure and development plan, including clear accountabilities, decision rights, and recruitment priorities to support the company’s growth agenda.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Partnership with the President

Serve as the President’s principal financial and strategic advisor, bringing CFO-level judgment to enterprise priorities, capital allocation, risk assessment, and growth decisions.
Lead enterprise planning and build integrated financial models that support growth initiatives, including new product launches, market expansion into the US and beyond, and investment decisions.
Evaluate strategic partnerships, joint ventures, licensing arrangements, and potential acquisitions, presenting clear, evidence-based recommendations to leadership.
Bring a commercial point of view to pricing, margin, and deal structure, especially on large institutional and government tenders.
Act as a credible financial voice with the board, shareholders, lenders, investors, and external advisors as the company matures and its stakeholder environment becomes more complex.

Capital Strategy, Banking & Investor Relations

Lead the company’s capital strategy, including banking relationships, lender negotiations, credit facilities, working capital planning, and financing structures aligned to the company’s growth ambitions.
Lead any future capital raise or strategic financing process, including the investment narrative, financial model, diligence materials, stakeholder communication, and data room readiness.
Identify and secure government funding, grants, tax credits (including SR&ED), and other non-dilutive capital available to Canadian manufacturers.
Maintain disciplined cash flow management and rolling forecasts that provide leadership with timely visibility into financial risks, opportunities, and capital requirements.

Financial Leadership, Operations & Reporting

Lead month-end and year-end close, and deliver accurate, timely financial statements.
Establish an annual planning, budgeting, forecasting, and performance management cadence that enables disciplined executive decision-making.
Establish a management reporting package with meaningful manufacturing KPIs, including gross margin by product, unit economics, inventory turns, working capital, and capacity utilization.
Oversee accounts payable, receivable, payroll, and treasury, and tighten controls as volume grows.
Coordinate the annual audit or review with external accountants.

Manufacturing Finance & Cost Management

Build a clear, reliable product costing model covering raw materials, labour, overhead, and yield.
Partner with operations on procurement, inventory planning, and capital equipment decisions, with the return on each investment clearly understood.
Identify and advance margin improvement opportunities across procurement, supply chain, production, and inventory management.
Manage foreign exchange and commodity exposure tied to raw materials and export sales.

Tax, Compliance & Risk

Oversee corporate tax, GST/HST/PST, and cross-border tax matters as the company sells into new jurisdictions.
Keep the company compliant with lender covenants, contract obligations, and financial reporting requirements.
Build out risk management, insurance, and internal controls appropriate for a company of Vitacore’s size and ambition.

Systems & Team

Assess current accounting and ERP systems and lead upgrades that give the business better, faster information.
Hire, develop, and lead a small, capable finance team, and build it thoughtfully as the company grows.
Implement practical, scalable processes that strengthen cross-functional accountability and support disciplined execution across the business.

What You Bring

15+ years of progressive finance leadership experience, including senior accountability as a CFO, VP Finance, Head of Finance, or finance executive with enterprise-wide responsibility.
CPA designation (CPA, CA, CMA, or CGA).
Experience in manufacturing, distribution, medical devices, or another product-based environment, with strong command of costing, inventory, and operational finance.
A track record in a founder-led or privately held company in the growth stage, ideally in the $10 million to $100 million range.
Demonstrated experience leading capital strategy, banking relationships, financing processes, and ideally equity raises, M&A, investor relations, or government funding programs.
Comfort operating at both strategic and detailed levels, from executive decision support to the hands-on financial work required in a growing business.
Advanced financial modelling, scenario planning, and executive communication skills, with the ability to translate complex analysis into clear business recommendations.
Exposure to US or international markets is a strong asset.

SALARY

$165,000–$185,000, commensurate with experience.

Who Will Thrive Here

The successful candidate will bring an ownership mindset and the stature to operate as a true member of the executive leadership team. They will view finance as a strategic lever for enterprise value creation and will be commercially astute, analytically rigorous, and confident advising an entrepreneurial President whose pace requires both responsiveness and disciplined challenge.

This is an environment for a builder: a finance leader who can design the systems, processes, reporting cadence, and team structure required for scale. The ideal candidate will be resourceful, pragmatic, and mission-aligned, with the credibility to operate at the executive level and the willingness to engage where the work is most critical.

WHY JOIN VITACORE

This is a compelling opportunity for a CFO to shape the financial foundation, strategic direction, and governance maturity of a Canadian manufacturer with a meaningful origin story and a clear growth mandate. The successful candidate will play a central role in enabling scale, improving enterprise performance, supporting capital decisions, and building the financial infrastructure required for Vitacore’s next stage of development.

jobs.title: Director, Artificial Intelligence, Finance
jobs.description:
Overview

AtkinsRéalis is looking for a Director, Artificial Intelligence, Finance to turn the potential of AI into measurable improvements in how Finance works and how the business makes decisions.

This is a hands-on leadership role. The Director will define a practical AI strategy, identify the opportunities worth pursuing and lead a disciplined portfolio from business case through adoption and verified results. They will also personally design, build, test and help deploy practical Finance agents and AI-enabled workflows within approved enterprise environments.

Success means tangible outcomes: capacity released for higher-value work, faster and better-informed decisions, stronger controls, improved cash performance and protection of project margins. The role is not about deploying technology for its own sake or accumulating pilots that never change how Finance operates.

Leading a small team with a global mandate, the Director will bring together Finance leaders and process owners with the Financial Systems Centre of Excellence (CoE), IT, Global Digital, the Chief Digital Officer's'organization, and data, cybersecurity, privacy and risk specialists. They will develop Finance-specific strategy and governance within enterprise standards, not create competing platforms or policies.

You are a business-led AI and transformation leader who combines strategic ambition, financial discipline and genuine hands-on ability. You can inspire executives, challenge a weak business case and align Finance, Digital, IT and control teams. You are as comfortable discussing strategy as you are building an agent to test an idea with users.

Your role

Set The Strategy And Build Alignment

Define and communicate a value-first AI strategy and roadmap for Global Finance, aligned with Finance priorities, enterprise AI strategy, technology standards and the Financial Systems roadmap.
Determine where AI can materially improve outcomes, where conventional automation or process redesign is preferable, and where an opportunity should not proceed.
Build a shared agenda across FP&A, Controllership, Project Finance and other Finance teams; engage regional and business leaders to identify needs that can scale.
Advise Finance leadership on investment choices, dependencies and risks; secure sponsorship and rally teams that do not report to the Director.

Own a Disciplined Portfolio Of Use Cases

Establish transparent intake and prioritization connected to enterprise channels and governance; assess business value, process and data readiness, feasibility, adoption, total cost and risk.
Maintain a sequenced portfolio with named sponsors, accountable process owners, delivery partners, milestones and clear decisions to proceed, change direction or stop.
Prioritize a few opportunities with a credible path to impact over a large collection of pilots. Candidate areas include reporting commentary, Finance knowledge access, exception handling, forecasting support, collections and project-margin early warning; each requires its own assessment and business case.

Make The Business Case And Prove The Return

Require proportionate business cases before material investment, with baselines, expected benefits, implementation and ongoing costs, risks, dependencies, adoption assumptions and alternatives.
Distinguish time saved from capacity genuinely redeployed and from cost removed; do not treat these as interchangeable financial benefits.
Agree measurement methods and benefit owners before delivery; track investment and realized value at use-case and portfolio levels, with independent validation where appropriate.
Report candidly on adoption, net value, cost and control effectiveness; recommend whether to improve, scale or discontinue initiatives that underperform.

Build, Test And Demonstrate Solutions Personally

Personally design, build and refine selected Finance agents and AI-enabled workflows, especially early prototypes and focused solutions that accelerate learning.
Use Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Studio hands-on to configure agents, test them with users, assess reliability and improve outputs based on feedback.
Use AI tools regularly in professional work to improve analysis, research, drafting and workflow execution, applying appropriate review and data-handling requirements.
Turn Finance problems into working demonstrations; assess limitations and costs, and decide whether a solution should stop, improve or enter the approved production route.
Stay close enough to delivery to challenge designs, troubleshoot barriers and coach builders, without being the sole developer of enterprise-scale products; partner with Digital and IT on supported deployment.

Establish Practical, Responsible Governance

Translate enterprise AI policy and standards into a Finance operating model covering ownership, intake, risk assessment, testing, approvals, human oversight, monitoring and lifecycle management.
Partner with Digital, IT, the Chief Digital Officer's'organization, Cybersecurity, Privacy, Legal, Risk and Internal Audit to clarify decision rights and navigate the path from idea to approved production use.
Protect sensitive Finance and client information through appropriate access, validation, traceability and human review before AI outputs inform reporting or decisions.
Work with data and process owners on source quality, definitions and controls; reuse approved enterprise platforms and challenge unnecessary complexity without bypassing security or technology accountabilities.

Deliver Through Partnership And Adoption

Partner with the Financial Systems CoE so initiatives fit ERP, EPM and reporting architecture without creating competing technology roadmaps.
Agree delivery responsibilities with Digital and IT while retaining Finance accountability for business outcomes; redesign workflows with process owners around human decisions, exceptions and controls.
Lead communications, training and feedback to build user confidence; create reusable approaches that can scale across regions while respecting genuine process and risk differences.

Lead a Lean, High-impact Team

Build and coach a small team with commercial judgment, hands-on capability and delivery discipline; mobilize a federated network of Finance champions, process owners and enterprise specialists.
Create a culture of curiosity, constructive challenge, accountability and collaboration, including the confidence to recommend "not AI" when appropriate.
Represent Finance in enterprise AI forums and lead by example as both sponsor and practitioner: demonstrate tools, share what works and acknowledge limitations.

About You

A degree in Finance, Business, Technology, Engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience, is expected.
Significant experience leading AI, data, automation or digital transformation in a complex organization, with demonstrated outcomes beyond proofs of concept.
Experience navigating architecture, cybersecurity, privacy, data governance and risk requirements without losing sight of business value or delivery pace.
Deeper practical experience with Copilot Cowork or Claude Cowork, including a proven record of deploying agentic workflows and demonstrating value in another organization.
Demonstrated hands-on experience building, testing and deploying AI agents, preferably in Microsoft Copilot Studio, with examples you personally created or materially developed.
Experience in an engineering, professional-services or project-based business; familiarity with enterprise Finance platforms, including Oracle-based environments.
Working knowledge of generative AI, agents, analytics and intelligent automation, sufficient to build focused solutions and challenge complex technical designs.
Strong understanding of Finance processes and decisions, ideally including FP&A, reporting, project or contract performance, working capital and financial controls.
Evidence of moving solutions beyond demonstrations to adoption, changed workflows and measurable business outcomes.
Active, capable use of Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT or Claude in day-to-day professional work, with sound judgment about approved tools, sensitive information and human review.
Proven ability to build investment cases, evaluate total cost and alternatives, establish benefit baselines and demonstrate return on investment.
Exceptional collaboration, executive communication and matrix leadership skills; sound judgment about when to scale, simplify or stop.

Rewards & benefits

Explore the rewards and benefits that help you thrive – at every stage of your life and your career at AtkinsRéalis in Canada.

Enjoy competitive compensation, employee recognition, and a brilliant range of flexible benefits you can tailor to your health, wellbeing, financial and lifestyle needs.

Make the most of diverse opportunities for training and professional development to grow your skills and expertise.

And take advantage of our hybrid working culture and generous time-off policies to balance a fulfilling career with your personal life.

Be rewarded. Find out more.

We're AtkinsRéalis, a world-class engineering services and nuclear organization. We connect people, data and technology to transform the world's'infrastructure and energy systems. We're committed to leading our clients across our various end markets to engineer a better future for our planet and its people.

This is an exceptional opportunity for a talented and results-oriented leader to make a significant impact in shaping our company's future and driving data-driven solutions in the evolving digital landscape. If you are passionate about data, AI, and strategic consulting, we invite you to apply and join our high-performing team.

Partner with clients to identify their business challenges and design tailored Data, AI & Cloud solutions
Oversee the delivery of high-quality data-driven insights, models, and strategic recommendations
Provide thought leadership and build trusted advisor relationships with key client stakeholders

Clear and tested experience in leading cross-functional teams and managing P&L responsibilities

jobs.description:
About Citi:

Citi, the leading global bank, has approximately 200 million customer accounts and does business in more than 160 countries and jurisdictions. Citi provides consumers, corporations, governments, and institutions with a broad range of financial products and services, including consumer banking and credit, corporate and investment banking, securities brokerage, transaction services, and wealth management.

As a bank with a brain and a soul, Citi creates economic value that is systemically responsible and in our clients’ best interests. As a financial institution that touches every region of the world and every sector that shapes your daily life, our Enterprise Operations & Technology teams are charged with a mission that rivals any large tech company. Our technology solutions are the foundations of everything we do from keeping the bank safe, managing global resources, and providing the technical tools our workers need to be successful to designing our digital architecture and ensuring our platforms provide a first-class customer experience. We reimagine client and partner experiences to deliver excellence through secure, reliable, and efficient services.

Our commitment to diversity includes a workforce that represents the clients we serve from all walks of life, backgrounds, and origins. We foster an environment where the best people want to work. We value and demand respect for others, promote individuals based on merit, and ensure opportunities for personal development are widely available to all. Ideal candidates are innovators with well-rounded backgrounds who bring their authentic selves to work and complement our culture of delivering results with pride. If you are a problem solver who seeks passion in your work, come join us. We’ll enable growth and progress together.

About the Team:

Citi is looking for a Lead AI/ML Data Scientist
to join the Olympus Data Reconciliation and Engineering team, where you will shape the next generation of AI and machine learning capabilities powering enterprise-scale reconciliation across global processing hubs.

In this role, you will drive the full lifecycle of ML model development — from ideation and architecture through to deployment and adoption — delivering measurable impact across Capital Markets operations, risk, and finance. Your work will sit at the intersection of advanced data science and real-world financial systems, influencing outcomes at a global scale.

Responsibilities:

Design, build, and deploy AI and machine learning models — including Agentic AI and Generative AI solutions — to solve complex reconciliation and data engineering challenges at enterprise scale.
Lead the end-to-end ML model development lifecycle, from requirements gathering and data preprocessing through to ensemble modeling, validation, and production integration.
Analyze large volumes of structured and unstructured financial data to uncover trends, patterns, and opportunities for optimization across banking platforms.
Define and deliver ML model roadmaps in collaboration with technical and business teams, ensuring alignment with project timelines, budgets, and Citi's architecture standards.
Translate complex data findings into clear visualizations and strategic recommendations that inform decisions made by senior business and technology leaders.
Partner with engineering, operations, and cross-functional teams to ensure seamless model integration, long-term scalability, and reliable performance in production environments.
Identify and communicate technology risks and their business implications, developing mitigation strategies and maintaining transparency with stakeholders at all levels.
Maintain comprehensive model documentation and support knowledge transfer to ensure continuity and adoption across teams.

Required Qualifications & Skills:

Technical Expertise:

6+ years hands-on experience in AI/ML development and big data engineering within Financial Services, Insurance, or Telecom environments
Expert-level proficiency in Python (scikit-learn, TensorFlow, PyTorch, Pandas, NumPy), R (caret, tidyverse, mlr3), and SQL (PostgreSQL, Oracle, MySQL)
Deep technical knowledge implementing supervised and unsupervised ML algorithms: linear/logistic regression, neural networks (CNN, RNN, LSTM, Transformers), k-means clustering, DBSCAN, decision trees (CART, C4.5), and ensemble methods (Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost)
Proven experience building and deploying Agentic AI and LLM-based solutions using:
LangGraph for complex agent orchestration and state management
LangChain for chain-of-thought reasoning and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
Agent Development Kit (ADK) for enterprise-grade autonomous agent development

Beneficial Skills & Qualifications:

Hands-on experience with advanced statistical modeling: Generalized Linear Models (GLM), Random Forest, Gradient Boosting (AdaBoost, XGBoost), and Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques including text mining, topic modeling (LDA), and sentiment analysis
Experience with model versioning and experiment tracking tools (Mlflow, Weights & Biases, DVC)
Proficiency with Git/GitHub/Bitbucket for version control and collaborative development
Knowledge of CI/CD pipelines for ML model deployment (Jenkins, GitLab CI, GitHub Actions)
Familiarity with data visualization libraries (Matplotlib, Seaborn, Plotly) and BI tools (Tableau, Power BI)
Experience with real-time streaming data frameworks (Kafka, Kinesis)
Passion for staying current with emerging AI/ML frameworks, research papers, and open-source contributions

Education:

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science
, Data Science
, Software Engineering
, Information Systems
, Mathematics
, Statistics
or related fields of study.

jobs.title: Director, Platform Product Owner
jobs.description:
Requisition ID: 274773

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

The Team

Global Wealth Banking and Markets Engineering (GWBMT) is the fast-moving, award-winning technology engine that powers Scotiabank's Wealth and Capital Markets businesses.

The Platform Engineering organization provides the foundational technology platforms and cloud services that enable application teams to innovate rapidly, securely, and at scale. Our portfolio includes enterprise Kubernetes platforms spanning on-premises and Google Cloud environments, Cloud Enablement Services, Kafka as a Service, Airflow as a Service, Fine-Grained Access Management capabilities, and future developer platform offerings that accelerate application modernization and cloud adoption.

The Role

We are seeking a Director Platform Product Owner to lead the product strategy, roadmap, adoption, and delivery of a portfolio of enterprise platform products that serve hundreds of engineers and mission-critical applications across the bank.

This role sits at the intersection of technology, product management, engineering, and business strategy. The successful candidate will be responsible for defining and evolving platform products that enable cloud adoption, application modernization, developer productivity, security, and operational excellence.

As a senior product leader, you will partner closely with Platform Engineering, Architecture, Security, Infrastructure, and application development teams to ensure our platforms deliver measurable business value, exceptional user experiences, and scalable solutions that meet the needs of a rapidly evolving enterprise landscape.

You will act as the voice of the engineering customer while balancing engineering priorities, platform sustainability, risk management, and strategic technology objectives.

Is this role right for you? In this role you will:

Product Strategy & Portfolio Leadership
Define and execute the strategic vision, roadmap, and lifecycle management of a portfolio of platform engineering products and services.
Develop product strategies that accelerate cloud adoption, platform standardization, application modernization, and engineering productivity.
Identify emerging customer needs and market trends to drive innovation and platform evolution.
Establish product success metrics, adoption goals, customer satisfaction targets, and business outcomes.
Prioritize investments and roadmap initiatives based on business value, engineering impact, risk reduction, and operational efficiency.

Product Portfolio Includes

Enterprise Kubernetes Platforms (On-Prem and Google Cloud)
Cloud Enablement and Migration Services
Airflow as a Service
Kafka as a Service
Fine-Grained Access Management Platforms
Developer Platform Capabilities and Self-Service Engineering Solutions
Customer Engagement & Platform Adoption
Act as the primary advocate for platform consumers across GBM and enterprise engineering teams.
Build deep understanding of customer journeys, pain points, and platform adoption barriers.
Drive platform onboarding strategies and self-service experiences that improve developer productivity.
Partner with application teams to identify modernization opportunities and accelerate cloud migration initiatives.
Lead customer advisory forums, feedback programs, and adoption reviews to continually improve platform offerings.
Establish product analytics frameworks and measurable indicators to track platform utilization, customer outcomes, productivity gains, and business value realization.
Technical Product Ownership
Translate strategic objectives into clear product roadmaps, capabilities, requirements, and delivery plans.
Collaborate with architects and engineering teams to define platform capabilities, service offerings, APIs, and user experiences.
Ensure platform products align with enterprise architecture standards, security requirements, and regulatory obligations.
Define service offerings, operating models, support models, and service-level objectives (SLOs) for platform products.
Champion platform engineering principles, self-service capabilities, automation, and developer experience improvements.
Establish service consumption metrics, cost transparency models, showback/chargeback capabilities, and platform ROI measures.
Delivery Leadership & Execution
Lead the planning and execution of platform product initiatives from ideation through delivery and adoption.
Partner with engineering leaders to balance feature development, platform reliability, technical debt reduction, and operational excellence.
Drive agile product delivery practices, roadmap governance, backlog prioritization, and release planning.
Track delivery performance and ensure successful execution of strategic initiatives across multiple platform teams.
Manage dependencies, risks, and stakeholder expectations across a complex enterprise environment.
Platform Reliability, Security & Operational Excellence
Define and monitor key platform performance indicators, including availability, reliability, scalability, security, adoption, and customer satisfaction.
Partner with Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), Security, and Operations teams to improve platform resiliency and operational maturity.
Ensure security controls, access governance, and compliance requirements are embedded within platform services.
Drive continual improvement initiatives focused on automation, observability, service health, and cost optimization.
Balance innovation with operational stability and risk management.
Own the end-to-end platform user experience across onboarding, self-service workflows, documentation, observability, support engagement, and lifecycle management.
Stakeholder Management & Executive Communication
Build strong relationships with senior technology leaders, architects, engineering teams, security stakeholders, and business partners.
Present product strategy, investment priorities, roadmap progress, and platform value realization to executive leadership.
Influence strategic technology decisions across cloud, platform engineering, developer experience, and modernization initiatives.
Communicate complex technical concepts effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences.

Skills

Do you have the skills that will enable you to succeed in this role? We’d love to work with you if you have:

10+ years of technology experience with at least 5 years in Product Management, Platform Engineering, Cloud Engineering, Developer Platforms, or Infrastructure Services.
Proven experience leading the strategy, roadmap, and delivery of large-scale platform products.
Experience working with cloud platforms, enterprise infrastructure, and application modernization initiatives.
Strong understanding of platform engineering, developer experience, self-service platforms, and product operating models.
Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders and drive alignment across multiple organizations.
Experience leading cross-functional teams in complex enterprise environments.
Outstanding communication, stakeholder management, and executive presentation skills.
Strong strategic thinking, prioritization, and data-driven decision-making capabilities.

Technical Expertise

Strong understanding of Kubernetes and container platforms operating across hybrid-cloud environments.
Experience with public cloud platforms, preferably Google Cloud Platform (GCP).
Familiarity with event-driven architectures, Kafka, streaming platforms, and modern data infrastructure.
Understanding of workflow orchestration and data engineering platforms such as Apache Airflow.
Knowledge of Identity and Access Management, Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), Fine-Grained Authorization, and Zero Trust security principles.
Experience with CI/CD, Infrastructure as Code, platform automation, observability, and reliability engineering practices.
Understanding of platform security, risk management, compliance, and operational resilience requirements.

Preferred

Experience building or managing Internal Developer Platforms (IDPs) and self-service engineering ecosystems.
Background in Platform Engineering, Site Reliability Engineering, DevOps, Cloud Architecture, or Software Engineering.
Experience driving enterprise cloud transformation and migration programs.
Experience within financial services, capital markets, or other highly regulated industries.
Knowledge of Google Cloud technologies including GKE, networking, observability, and security services.

Success Measures

Success In This Role Will Be Measured By

Platform adoption and customer satisfaction
Growth of cloud-enabled and modernized applications
Developer productivity improvements and self-service adoption
Reliability, availability, and operational performance of platform services
Reduction in onboarding friction and time-to-market
Delivery of strategic roadmap commitments
Platform cost optimization and operational efficiency
Achievement of security, compliance, and risk management objectives

What's in it for you?

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion & Allyship - We strive to create an inclusive culture where every employee is empowered to reach their fullest potential, respected for who they are, and are embraced through bias-free practices and inclusive values across Scotiabank. We embrace diversity and provide opportunities for all employee to learn, grow & participate through our various Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) that span across diverse gender identities, ethnicity, race, age, ability & veterans.

Scotiabank continues to locate, remove, and prevent barriers so that we can build a diverse and inclusive environment while meeting accessibility requirements.
Upskilling through online courses, cross-functional development opportunities, and tuition assistance.
Competitive Rewards program including bonus, flexible vacation, personal, sick days, and benefits will start on day one.
Community Engagement - no matter where you choose to work from; we offer opportunities for community engagement & belonging with our various programs.

Guided by our purpose: "for every future", we help our customers, their families and their communities achieve success through a broad range of advice, products and services, including personal and commercial banking, wealth management and private banking, corporate and investment banking, and capital markets.

Directeur(trice) Principal(e) de la Technologie et de l'Innovation

À propos de Crowe BGK

Depuis 75 ans, Crowe BGK S.E.N.C.R.L. est un chef de file de confiance en matière de services de comptabilité et de conseil au Canada. Notre équipe compte plus de 250 professionnels qui servent nos clients à partir de nos bureaux de Montréal et d’Ottawa. Nous offrons des services d’audit, de fiscalité, de conseil et de consultation, aidant les particuliers et les sociétés privées à relever des défis complexes. Nous sommes fiers d’avoir été nommés parmi les 100 meilleurs employeurs de PME au Canada et parmi les meilleurs employeurs de Montréal, car nous croyons qu’il est essentiel de créer un milieu de travail où les gens se sentent soutenus, valorisés et inspirés à progresser.

Nous sommes à la recherche d’un(e) Directeur(trice) Principal(e) de la Technologie et de l'Innovation

expérimenté(e) et pratique pour aider Crowe BGK à maintenir un environnement technologique fiable et à faire progresser l’utilisation des logiciels à l’échelle du cabinet. La personne retenue combinera une compréhension des processus d’affaires, une discipline opérationnelle et une expertise technologique afin d’améliorer le service à la clientèle, l’efficacité, l’évolutivité et l’expérience employé.

Vous Serez Responsable De

Stratégie et gouvernance des logiciels d’entreprise

Élaborer et maintenir la feuille de route pluriannuelle des applications du cabinet, l’inventaire des logiciels, le modèle de propriété et la gouvernance pour la sélection, les accès, les changements, les intégrations, les renouvellements et le retrait.
Identifier les lacunes en matière de capacités, les dédoublements, les outils sous-utilisés ou non pris en charge ainsi que les occasions émergentes; conseiller le ou la COFO, les associé(e)s et la direction sur les priorités, les investissements, les compromis, la normalisation et les coûts.

Amélioration des processus d’affaires et innovation

Analyser et repenser les processus dans les services à la clientèle et les fonctions corporatives, en mobilisant les parties prenantes afin de résoudre les irritants, les lacunes de contrôle, le travail à refaire, les problèmes de données et les besoins non satisfaits avant l’automatisation.
Utiliser les données et les commentaires pour prioriser les améliorations à forte valeur ajoutée et évaluer les flux de travail, l’automatisation, l’analytique, l’intelligence artificielle et les technologies émergentes en tenant compte de la confidentialité, de la qualité, des contrôles et de la supervision humaine appropriés.

Évaluation des logiciels et analyses de rentabilité

Traduire les besoins d’affaires en exigences mesurables sur les plans fonctionnel, technique, des données, de la sécurité, de l’intégration, des contrôles, du service et des utilisateurs; diriger les démonstrations, les projets pilotes, les vérifications de références, les grilles d’évaluation, la diligence raisonnable des fournisseurs et la comparaison objective des risques et des solutions de rechange.
Préparer et présenter des analyses de rentabilité pour les décisions d’aller de l’avant ou non, couvrant le coût total de possession, le rendement du capital investi, les échéanciers, les ressources, l’incidence du changement, la formation, l’atténuation des risques, le soutien et les coûts de sortie; soutenir les négociations commerciales et contractuelles.

Gouvernance et responsabilité de la mise en œuvre

Agir à titre de responsable imputable du volet affaires et technologie, en partenariat avec le ou la gestionnaire de projet attitré(e), afin de définir la portée, les résultats, le budget, les ressources, la gouvernance, les jalons, les droits décisionnels, les risques, les communications et les mesures de succès.
Coordonner les parties prenantes et veiller à la conception des processus, à la configuration, aux intégrations, à la conversion des données, aux essais, aux contrôles, à la formation, à la mise en production, au soutien, à la préparation, à la stabilisation, à l’adoption et à la réalisation des bénéfices; faire remonter les lacunes importantes et maintenir la visibilité auprès de la direction.

Gestion du portefeuille, des fournisseurs, des données et des risques

Gérer les budgets logiciels, les licences, l’utilisation, les renouvellements, les fournisseurs, les contrats, les niveaux de service, les indicateurs du portefeuille, la rationalisation et le retrait des solutions.
Collaborer avec les ressources en TI, cybersécurité, protection de la vie privée, affaires juridiques et gestion des risques afin d’encadrer les intégrations, les données, les contrôles d’accès, la continuité des activités, les risques liés aux tiers, l’intelligence artificielle et l’automatisation.

Leadership du changement et mobilisation des parties prenantes

Établir des relations de confiance avec les associé(e)s, les dirigeant(e)s, le personnel, les fournisseurs et les prestataires de services; diriger les employé(e)s attitré(e)s et les équipes interfonctionnelles en assurant une responsabilisation claire et une forte orientation vers le service.
Diriger les communications, la formation, l’adoption, la documentation, le soutien et la propriété des applications; développer des ambassadeurs internes, contribuer au plan d’affaires du cabinet et tenir le ou la COFO ainsi que les parties prenantes informés.

Autorité et responsabilité

Responsable du portefeuille de logiciels, de la feuille de route des applications, des normes de gouvernance et de la direction des équipes de mise en œuvre des TI et des processus dans le cadre de la stratégie et des budgets approuvés; peut exiger les examens appropriés en matière d’affaires, de sécurité, de protection de la vie privée, d’intégration, de contrôle et de mise en œuvre.
Recommande la sélection, le séquencement, le renouvellement, l’expansion, la consolidation ou le retrait des logiciels; peut suspendre ou faire remonter les préoccupations non résolues et est responsable de la qualité des recommandations, de la gouvernance de la mise en œuvre, de l’adoption, de la stabilisation et des bénéfices approuvés.

Mesures de succès

Gérer un inventaire à jour des logiciels, une propriété claire, une gouvernance rigoureuse, une feuille de route approuvée, des analyses de rentabilité crédibles et des dépenses contrôlées.
Réaliser les mises en œuvre avec une gouvernance, une préparation, des contrôles, une adoption et un soutien durable efficaces, ainsi qu’avec la réalisation des bénéfices approuvés.
Obtenir des améliorations mesurables en matière d’efficacité, de capacité, de qualité, de fiabilité des données, d’expérience employé et client, de performance des fournisseurs, de gestion des risques et de confiance des parties prenantes.

Les Qualifications Qui Comptent

Baccalauréat en systèmes d’information, administration des affaires, comptabilité, finance, informatique, génie ou dans un domaine connexe; une combinaison équivalente de formation et d’expérience sera considérée.
Sept années ou plus d’expérience progressive en logiciels, systèmes d’affaires, amélioration des processus, transformation technologique, gestion de produits ou gestion de programmes, dont au moins trois années dans un rôle de leadership ou de responsabilité à l’échelle de l’entreprise.
Une expérience dans un cabinet comptable ou un autre environnement de services professionnels est privilégiée, avec une compréhension des décisions dirigées par les associé(e)s, du service à la clientèle soumis à des échéanciers, de la confidentialité et du changement entre les groupes de pratique.
Succès démontré dans la direction d’évaluations de logiciels, d’analyses de rentabilité, de sélection de fournisseurs et de mise en œuvre de solutions SaaS à l’échelle du cabinet ou de l’entreprise.
Expérience pratique de la cartographie et de la refonte des processus, des exigences, des essais, de la formation, de la gestion du changement et de la réalisation des bénéfices.

jobs.title: Director Technical Solutions - Digital
jobs.description:
Permanent Full Time

Director, Technical Solutions

Our Digital Strategy and Design team is looking for a Director, Technical Solutions
to lead the delivery of high-quality digital solutions in partnership with business and technology teams.

This hands-on technology leader will guide solutions from design through production, set engineering direction and work with architecture, cybersecurity and enterprise platform teams to deliver secure, reliable outcomes.

What you will do:

In this role, you will co-lead a cross-functional team with the Product Owner, translating product outcomes into an executable technical plan and remaining close enough to the work to guide design, code, integration, testing, release and production support.

You will establish reusable engineering foundations, automated quality and security controls, and operational practices that increase delivery speed, improve reliability and reduce duplication across teams. Key accountabilities will also include the following:

Own end-to-end technical delivery across experience, application, API, integration, data and cloud layers, making pragmatic design decisions within enterprise architecture guardrails
Remain hands-on through architecture spikes, code and design reviews, troubleshooting automation and critical-path delivery while enabling engineers to own implementation
Apply AI-based technologies where they create measurable value, including generative AI, intelligent automation and AI-assisted software delivery, with appropriate data, privacy, security, model-risk and human-oversight controls
Establish full-stack engineering standards for user experience, accessability, performance, API design, data handling, observability, testing and maintainability

What you will bring:

Degree/diploma in computer science or related discipline, or equivalent combination of training and experience
A minimum of 10+ years’ related experience delivering digital products and technology platforms, including accountability for solution design, engineering execution, release and production health
Deep technologist with recent hands-on software delivery experience in roles such as Engineering Lead, Technical Lead or Solutions Architect
Demonstrated full-stack expertise across modern web or mobile experiences, backend services, APIs, integrations, data stores and cloud infrastructure
Strong understanding of distributed-system design, including event-driven architecture, microservices, consistency, scalability, resiliency, observability and failure recovery
Experience applying AI-based technologies—including generative AI or machine learning capabilities—to production use cases, with knowledge of responsible AI, privacy, security, data quality, evaluation and monitoring
Demonstrated ability to make and communicate technical trade-offs across scope, time, cost, risk, quality and long-term maintainability
Experience working in a complex, regulated and rapidly evolving environment with high expectations for security, reliability and execution
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical decisions, options and risks to technical and non-technical audiences

Assets:

Experience in financial services, preferably insurance
Experience modernizing applications, decomposing and rationalizing systems, and integrating with core or legacy platforms
Experience delivering omnichannel experiences using cloud-native architecture
Knowledge of business and continuous architecture practices, architecture modelling tools and frameworks such as UML, ArchiMate and TOGAF; TOGAF certification is an asset

The base salary for this position is between $149,000 - $199,000
annually. This represents base salary only and does not represent other variable compensation components of our total compensation ( i.e. annual bonus, commission etc). If you are selected to move forward in our recruitment process, your recruiter will be able to discuss additional details of our total rewards program with you.

jobs.description:
The Klick Group
—comprising Klick Health (including Klick Katalyst and btwelve), Klick Media Group, Klick Applied Sciences (including Klick Labs), Klick Consulting, and Klick Ventures—is an ecosystem dedicated to realizing the full potential of our people and clients in life sciences. Founded in 1997, we have offices in New York, Philadelphia, Saratoga Springs, Toronto, London, São Paulo, and Singapore. Consistently named a Best Managed Company, Most Admired Corporate Culture, and Great Place to Work, Klick is committed to fostering a high-performance, people-first culture with creativity, collaboration, innovation, and impact across everything we do.

About Our Technology Craft

Our Technology Craft powers Klick’s innovation through platforms, products, and emerging technologies. This craft enables scale, efficiency, and experimentation across the business. Technology teams transform ideas into functional, future-ready solutions. Their work supports both client delivery and internal growth.

Job Description

The Vice President, Enterprise Platforms leads enterprise architecture, client solutioning, and pre-sales strategy for pharmaceutical and life sciences organizations. This role bridges sales opportunity ownership with hands-on technical leadership, shaping complex omnichannel ecosystems that drive measurable business impact. The position partners closely with Sales, Strategy, Medical, Media, and Delivery teams to position technology as a differentiator in multi-million-dollar pursuits while establishing scalable architecture standards.

What You’ll Do

Lead enterprise pre-sales strategy, pipeline forecasting, and opportunity management for multi-million-dollar pharmaceutical platform engagements in collaboration with Sales and Account teams.
Facilitate executive discovery workshops and roadmap sessions with senior pharma stakeholders to define CRM, marketing automation, and data architecture strategies.
Design end-to-end omnichannel architectures spanning Salesforce, Veeva, Adobe, Marketo, SFMC, Snowflake, Databricks, Fabric, CDPs, APIs, and integration layers.
Produce architecture diagrams, interaction models, data flows, solution specifications, pricing estimates, and SOW documentation aligned to client and delivery requirements.
Establish governance frameworks, architecture standards, and AI-enabled solution patterns while guiding steering committees and mentoring internal architecture teams.

Qualifications

Required:

10+ years of experience in pharmaceutical or life sciences technology, consulting, or enterprise sales operations with demonstrated ownership of complex client engagements.
5+ years of hands-on enterprise architecture or solution design experience, including documented architecture diagrams, data models, and technical specifications.
Proven experience leading pre-sales efforts and managing pipeline for multi-million-dollar opportunities, including forecasting and proposal development.
Deep expertise in enterprise platforms such as Salesforce, Veeva, Adobe Experience Cloud, Marketo, SFMC, Snowflake, Databricks, Microsoft Fabric, or comparable ecosystems.
Demonstrated experience presenting technical strategies and architecture roadmaps to senior client stakeholders and executive steering committees.

Desired:

Comfort and enthusiasm for using AI as a regular part of how work gets done.
Experience applying AI/ML solutions such as next-best-action, personalization models, predictive analytics, or generative AI for content modularization and insight automation.
Formal training or certification in architecture frameworks such as TOGAF, SAFe, or equivalent enterprise methodologies.
Experience establishing architecture governance processes and reference models within regulated industries.

Additional Information

This posting is for an existing vacancy at Klick.

Our Commitment to Inclusion

Klick is consciously creating a culture where everyone can thrive and grow in their careers. We believe that our best work comes from our diverse backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. We strongly encourage members of historically underrepresented communities to apply, including Black people, Indigenous peoples, and other people of color, people with disabilities, people from gender and sexually diverse communities and people with intersectional identities. jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
Your CFO Opportunity Starts Here

Ready for the Seat You've Been Working Toward?

Not every great CFO starts with the title.

Many earn it through leadership, execution, business acumen, and the ability to help an organization reach its next level.

If you're a VP Finance, Director of Finance, or rising finance leader who has been waiting for the right opportunity to step into a CFO role, this may be exactly what you've been looking for.

Beam is seeking an ambitious, strategic, and hands-on Chief Financial Officer who wants to make a meaningful impact on a growing healthcare organization. This is a unique opportunity to join a collaborative leadership team, work directly with the CEO, and help shape the future of a dynamic, physician-led business.

We believe great CFOs are more than financial experts. They're business leaders. They influence strategy. They develop people. They create accountability. They see opportunities others miss. They help organizations grow.

This role is ideal for someone who wants to roll up their sleeves, build credibility, drive results, and ultimately prove they belong at the executive leadership table.

You'll have responsibility for Finance, Accounting, Billing, Revenue Cycle, Treasury, Financial Planning & Analysis, Physician Compensation, and Information Technology, while helping lead strategic planning, operational performance, and organizational growth.

If you're looking for a role where you can build, lead, influence, and leave your mark, we'd like to meet you.

ROLE MANDATE

The CFO is responsible for leading the organization's accounting, financial reporting, and treasury functions, ensuring the delivery of accurate, timely, and meaningful financial information while maintaining strong internal controls and disciplined financial management practices.
As a hands-on member of the senior leadership team, the CFO serves as a trusted business partner, providing reliable financial reporting, budgeting and forecasting, cash flow oversight, and business analysis to support strategic decision-making, operational excellence, and the achievement of the organization's objectives.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Own the monthly, quarterly and annual financial close and ensure accurate, timely financial statements.
Lead general accounting, accounts payable, accounts receivable, payroll oversight, reconciliations and the general ledger.
Maintain accounting policies, internal controls and approval processes; identify and remediate control weaknesses.
Coordinate the annual external audit and support tax compliance, regulatory reporting and year-end requirements.
Prepare annual budgets, forecasts, variance analysis and recurring management.
Monitor cash balances, working capital, collections and payment processes; support treasury and banking administration.
Lead and develop the accounting team while improving processes, documentation, systems and automation.

SHORT TERM PRIORITIES

Standardize and accelerate the month-end close with dependable reporting deadlines.
Strengthen reconciliations, internal controls, accounting policies and financial documentation.
Improve accounts receivable, collections, working-capital reporting and cash visibility.
Build useful budget-to-actual and location/service profitability reporting.
Assess accounting team responsibilities and identify opportunities for system and process automation.

CANDIDATE PROFILE

CPA designation strongly preferred.
Approximately 6-12+ years of progressive accounting and finance experience, including Controller, Assistant Controller or senior finance leadership experience.
Strong technical accounting, financial reporting, controls and close-management capabilities.
Experience in a private, entrepreneurial or multi-location operating company preferred.
Hands-on leadership style with the ability to review detail while maintaining strong deadlines and accountability.
Advanced budgeting, forecasting, Excel and financial systems skills; experience improving ERP/reporting processes is an asset.
Healthcare or medical-sector experience is an asset, particularly with multi-location operations, billing or practitioner economics.
Clear communicator who can explain financial results to both finance and non-finance managers.
Proactive, hands-on, and willing to roll up their sleeves.
Strong leadership skills.
Able to think outside the box and find creative solutions.
High energy and driven.
Genuinely passionate about healthcare, MedTech, and innovation.

MEASURES OF SUCCESS

Accurate and timely reporting
Faster and disciplined close
Strong controls and reconciliations
Improved collections and working capital
Reliable budgets and forecasts
Efficient accounting processes
A capable and accountable finance team

WHY JOIN BEAM?

This is more than a CFO role. It's an opportunity to step into a key leadership position, partner directly with the CEO, and help shape the future of a growing healthcare organization. If you're ready to build, lead, influence, and make a lasting impact, we encourage you to apply.

EQUITY, DIVERSITY & INCLUSION

Beam Radiology is committed to fostering an inclusive, respectful, and equitable workplace. We welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds, including Indigenous Peoples, racialized communities, persons with disabilities, members of the LGBTQ2S+ community, and others who may contribute to the diversity of our team.

Accommodations are available throughout the recruitment process. If you require accommodation, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.

HOW TO APPLY

Please submit your resume and cover letter to: 📧 careers@beamradiology.com

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Chief Financial Officer based in Canada.

The Chief Financial Officer will lead the financial strategy and operations of a rapidly scaling technology business, helping shape its next stage of growth. This executive-level role combines strategic leadership with hands-on operational oversight across financial planning, accounting, reporting, and capital strategy. Working closely with the CEO, executive team, and Board, the CFO will strengthen financial discipline, improve decision-making, and build scalable systems and processes. The role requires a proven track record of scaling SaaS or technology companies, navigating complex financial milestones, and preparing organizations for future financing or strategic events. The successful candidate will develop a high-performing finance organization while ensuring reliable forecasting, robust controls, and credible financial reporting. This is a remote opportunity for a senior leader based in Canada or the United States, with required travel to Ottawa and Toronto.

Accountabilities

Lead and develop the FP&A and Accounting functions, establishing clear priorities, strengthening collaboration, and ensuring accurate, timely financial deliverables.
Assess existing financial operations, identify process gaps, and work directly with teams to resolve issues and improve operational effectiveness.
Simplify and document core finance processes, enhance data quality, and introduce automation to reduce manual effort, errors, and reliance on workarounds.
Oversee financial planning and analysis, including budgets, forecasts, financial models, and performance analysis, translating insights into actionable business decisions.
Direct accounting operations, financial close processes, audits, reporting, and internal controls while ensuring compliance with applicable GAAP and IFRS requirements.
Partner with the CEO and Board on financial strategy, capital requirements, financing opportunities, and investor communications.
Bring financial rigor to company-wide decisions involving pricing, investment, headcount, and market expansion.
Evaluate acquisitions and strategic partnerships, leading financial modelling, valuation, due diligence, and post-transaction integration planning.
Build and coach a finance organization capable of supporting significant revenue growth, with systems, controls, and talent aligned to long-term business needs.
Ensure forecasting, financial reporting, and Board materials are accurate, credible, and trusted by executive stakeholders.
Prepare the organization for future fundraising, financing, or other strategic milestones well in advance.

Requirements

10+ years of progressive finance leadership experience, including previous CFO experience within a scaling business.
Demonstrated success scaling SaaS or technology companies from approximately $50 million to more than $200 million in revenue, with experience navigating different exit paths.
Deep expertise in financial planning and analysis, including strategic planning, forecasting, financial modelling, and performance management.
Direct experience with late-stage fundraising, such as Series C, D, or E, or experience operating in public markets.
Strong understanding of SaaS metrics, recurring revenue models, and the financial drivers of technology businesses.
Solid knowledge of GAAP and IFRS, compliance frameworks, internal controls, and audit oversight.
Proven ability to lead, mentor, and develop high-performing finance teams and senior functional leaders.
Strong strategic judgment and analytical skills, with the ability to balance detailed operational problem-solving with a company-wide perspective.
Demonstrated ability to partner effectively with CEOs, executive teams, and Boards, influencing decisions through clear financial insights and sound judgment.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
The Aga Khan Museum connects cultures and communities through the arts. The Museum’s mission is to spark wonder, curiosity, and understanding of Muslim cultures and their connection with other cultures through the arts.

The Toronto-based Museum promotes pluralism through art, storytelling, and enlightened encounters across cultures. Using traditional and contemporary art as well as performing arts as a force for positive change, the Museum’s vision is to impact lives and contribute to more inclusive and peaceful societies. The Museum acts as a global learning hub, playing a unique and pivotal role in building connections between people and communities locally, nationally, and internationally.

Purpose of Position

Reporting to the Director & Chief Executive Officer, the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) is a key member of the Senior Leadership Team (SLT) responsible for the financial sustainability, stewardship, risk management and financial governance of the organization, while serving as a strategic advisor to the Director & CEO, Board of Directors, and SLT. The CFO also provides financial and strategic oversight of the Museum’s commercial activities.

Leadership Profile

The ideal candidate is a strategic and financially sophisticated executive who combines disciplined stewardship with sound commercial judgment. They are collaborative, analytical and results-oriented, with exceptional integrity, sound judgement and the ability to communicate complex financial matters clearly. They build strong relationships with the internal senior leaders and external partners and are capable of leading through change and complexity while advancing the Museum’s mission.

Ultimately, the CFO is responsible for safeguarding the organization's financial health and long-term sustainability.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership

Serve as a strategic advisor to the Director & CEO, SLT, and Board of Directors.
Serve as the principal management liaison with the Board, Finance & Audit Committee, and the Investment Committee by preparing and presenting financial information and recommendations, supporting Committee mandates, agendas and decision-making, advising the Board on significant financial risks and ensuring appropriate follow-up on Board and Committee decisions.
Foster collaboration, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement.
Build, develop and lead high-performing finance, procurement, and commercial teams with appropriate capabilities, succession, accountability and service orientation.

Financial Stewardship

Develop and maintain a long-term financial sustainability framework, including scenarios focused on funding, operating costs, reserves, liquidity and capital requirements aligned with the organizational strategy of the Museum.
Lead the annual budgeting, multi-year financial planning, forecasting, management reporting and financial performance analysis processes, ensuring that financial resources are aligned with the Museum’s strategic priorities.
Lead the Museum’s preparation for and coordination of the annual external financial statement audit, serving as the senior management liaison with the external auditors and ensuring the timely resolution and communication of significant audit matters, findings and recommendations.
Partner with the Development team to support fundraising and grant objectives through sound financial planning, proposal development and reporting, and ensure appropriate accounting and stewardship of restricted funds, grants, funding agreements and donor-designated resources.
Identify opportunities to enhance revenue, control costs, and improve Museum performance.

Risk, Compliance & Governance

Accountable for the integrity and timeliness of the Museum’s financial statements, management and Board reporting, accounting practices, internal controls, external audit and statutory and regulatory reporting.
Oversee treasury, liquidity, banking and financing arrangements, reserve strategy, investment governance and performance, and the financial planning and oversight of major capital requirements and projects.
Ensures the Museum maintains its tax-exempt charitable status and meets all related tax compliance requirements, including tax reporting, disbursement quotas, and dealings with the CRA.
Lead the Museum’s enterprise risk management framework and consolidated risk reporting, ensuring that significant financial, operational, insurance, legal, contractual, technology and other organizational risks have appropriate ownership, assessment and mitigation plans.
Coordinate the integration of enterprise risk management with business continuity planning and reporting to the Board and relevant Committees.
Provide executive oversight of procurement, ensuring appropriate policies, competitive practices, delegated authorities, contract controls and value for money.

Commercial Activities

Provide financial and strategic oversight of the Museum’s commercial activities.
Work with the responsible operational leaders to establish and monitor appropriate revenue, margin and performance targets and ensure effective financial controls and reporting.
Evaluate significant new commercial opportunities for financial viability, organizational capacity, risk and alignment with the Museum’s mission and strategic priorities.
Establish and monitor commercial performance targets.

Qualifications & Experience 

CPA designation.
MBA or graduate degree in business, finance, or a related field is an asset.
Minimum 10 years of progressive leadership experience, including at least five years in a senior financial leadership or executive role.
Proven expertise in financial leadership, strategic planning, organizational performance, risk management, and governance.
Experience providing financial and strategic oversight of commercial activities.
Experience presenting to Boards and leading multidisciplinary teams.
Nonprofit and/or charitable sector experience in arts, culture, hospitality, tourism, entertainment, education, or other mission-driven organizations preferred.

jobs.description:
Our client is a highly respected, mission-driven organization dedicated to improving well-being and quality of life in the communities it serves. The organization is seeking a strategic and forward-thinking Vice President, Finance to join its Executive Leadership Team. Reporting to the CEO, the Vice President will provide enterprise-wide leadership across Finance and corporate services, while serving as a trusted advisor to the CEO, Board of Directors, and senior leadership team.

The organization delivers essential services to a large and diverse client base. Behind every service are countless financial, operational, and strategic decisions that turn resources into meaningful impact. As Vice President, Finance, the successful candidate will ensure the financial strength, insight, and discipline needed to advance the mission and support long-term sustainability.

This is an exceptional opportunity for an accomplished finance executive who combines strategic insight with operational leadership and wants to influence meaningful outcomes in a purpose-driven organization. More than a functional leader, the Vice President will be a key enterprise partner, helping shape strategy, support growth, and position the organization for continued success in a complex operating environment.

The Mandate

The mandate extends well beyond traditional financial stewardship. As a member of the Executive Leadership Team, the VP will help shape organizational strategy, support evidence-based decision-making, and ensure the long-term sustainability of an organization delivering critical services.

In partnership with the CEO, Board, and senior leadership team, the VP will provide strategic financial leadership across planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, treasury, audit, risk management, and compliance. They will ensure financial resources are aligned with organizational priorities while maintaining the discipline and accountability the mission requires.

A key priority will be supporting the organization through a period of growth and change. Using financial insights and performance data, the VP will help evaluate opportunities, inform strategic initiatives, and optimize the deployment of resources in a complex funding and operating environment. Success will require balancing long-term vision with disciplined execution and sound financial management.

Beyond finance, the VP will provide executive oversight of key corporate services, including procurement and facilities, ensuring effective stewardship of organizational resources and infrastructure. The role will also lead efforts to strengthen internal capabilities, foster collaboration across departments, and build a high-performing, engaged team.

The successful candidate will have the opportunity to evolve the finance function from a trusted service provider into an even more proactive strategic partner and to enable data-driven decision-making across the organization. Success will be measured not only by financial outcomes, but also by the ability to influence strategy, support growth, and contribute to long-term sustainability and impact.

Leadership and Stewardship

The organization is seeking a VP Finance who leads with maturity and earns trust through action. This is not a role for someone who relies on title or tenure to get things done. The culture here rewards people who show up prepared, communicate clearly, and follow through.
Operates with humility, credibility, and sound judgment
Brings a practical, solutions-oriented mindset
Communicates clearly and influences at all levels
A good partner to the program managers – asking what they need before explaining what the number say
Leads with integrity, accountability, and transparency

Ideal Background

The successful candidate will bring experience in social services, healthcare, the boarder public sector, or the not-for-profit sector. Those who understand the operational, funding, and stakeholder dynamics of publicly funded organizations will be particular well positioned for success.
A CPA designation and progressive senior finance leadership experience.
Experience leading finance within a complex, multi-stakeholder organization.
A strong understanding of financial planning, financial reporting, treasury, governance, risk management, and internal controls.
Experience working with Boards and senior executives in a strategic advisory capacity.
The ability to translate financial information into actionable business insights.
A collaborative leadership style and a reputation for building strong relationships across an organization.

Why This Role

This is a rare opportunity to combine executive-level impact with genuine purpose. As a strategic partner to the CEO and Executive Leadership Team, the Vice President, Finance will help shape decisions that influence the organization’s direction, sustainability, and growth.

The successful candidate will join an organization at an exciting point in its journey, with the opportunity to strengthen financial stewardship, support strategic priorities, and help position the organization for continued success. The organization measures its success not only by financial performance, but by the positive impact it has on the people and communities it serves.

If you are ready to make a meaningful impact and help shape the future of a mission-driven organization, we encourage you to apply in confidence.

Leading the process of developing the department's annual budget, working with program managers and finance staff to gather input, projections, and cost estimates;

Managing the process for budget amendments or revisions as necessary, providing clear justifications and seeking necessary approvals for changes;
Ensuring that all financial reports meet regulatory requirements and government accounting principles, providing transparency and accountability in financial disclosures;
Establishing and maintaining robust internal controls to safeguard financial assets, prevent fraud, and ensure the accuracy and integrity of financial data;
Overseeing and leading a team of financial professionals, providing guidance, mentorship, and support to promote their professional growth and ensure effective departmental operations;
Fostering a culture of collaboration and cross-functional teamwork, working closely with other department heads to ensure financial considerations are integrated into broader strategic planning.

Undergraduate degree in accounting, finance, business administration, economics, commerce, or related field;
Completion of a professional accounting designation CPA (CMA, CGA or CA);
Eight (8) years of related experience;
