How you will contribute to the team:

In conjunction with the Manager of Finance, oversee all accounts, ledgers, and reporting systems ensuring compliance with IFRS and regulatory requirements.
Maintain internal control and safeguards for receipt of revenue, costs, program budgets, and actual expenditures.

What you bring:

Strong understanding of economic and banking processes.
Keen analytic, organization and problem-solving skills which allows for strategic data interpretation versus simple reporting.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills; experience in effectively communicating key data, including presentations to senior management, board, or other outside partners.

Investing in Your Growth

Making a Difference Together

Crozier Social

From sports leagues and game nights to creative workshops and social events, there are plenty of opportunities to connect with colleagues. Throughout the year, we bring our teams together through activities such as golf tournaments, hikes, boat cruises, and other fun company-wide events.

Salary range:
$130,000 - $170,000

Omegro is an international buy-and-grow acquirer of software companies looking for a permanent and safe home to continue their legacy and provide long-term sustainable growth for their people, their businesses, and their stakeholders.

As we acquire, integrate and grow businesses, this role is suited to individuals who enjoy partnering with Finance Managers, General Managers, CEOs and wider leadership teams to translate strategy into practical plans, scalable frameworks and high-impact initiatives that support financial performance, disciplined execution and successful acquisitions. Chief Financial Officer

What will you bring?

You’ll thrive here if you have operated as a senior finance leader, can build trust quickly across diverse business leadership teams, enjoy turning complexity into clear, practical action, and bring strong judgement through data-led decision making and strategic business partnering. You are motivated by coaching others to succeed, creating accountability through clear communication, and helping Finance Managers build the capability, confidence and discipline needed to support high-performing businesses.

jobs.description:
About QuadReal Property Group

QuadReal Property Group is a global real estate investment, development and operating company headquartered in Vancouver, British Columbia. Its assets under management are $98.5 billion. From its foundation in Canada as a full-service real estate operating company, QuadReal has expanded its capabilities globally for investments in equity and debt in both the public and private markets. QuadReal invests directly through operating platforms in which it holds an ownership interest and via programmatic partnerships.

QuadReal seeks to deliver strong investment returns while creating sustainable environments that bring value to the people and communities it serves. Now and for generations to come.

QuadReal: Excellence lives here.

www.quadreal.com

Role Description

The Director, Enterprise Data Governance is accountable for defining and governing the enterprise data QuadReal relies on, anchored in DAMA-DMBOK, covering data definitions, ownership, quality, and observability. This makes QuadReal's data reliable enough to be governed, measured, and controlled, reducing the risk that decisions, reporting, and controls rest on data that can't be trusted. The role reports to the VP, Risk & Integrated Assurance and turns the VP's enterprise-wide mandate into one accountable operating model focused on risk mitigation through data governance lens.

Success is measured by the risk it mitigates: data issues caught before they become decisions made on incorrect information, ownership gaps closed before they become accountability gaps. Holding up under audit is one key aspect of that risk mitigation but not the goal in itself.

The Director also supports the VP's overall view of QuadReal's risk and control environment and represents Data Governance in Risk & Integrated Assurance reporting.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Data Governance
Define QuadReal’s enterprise data definitions, classifications, and Critical Data Elements (CDEs), anchored in DAMA-DMBOK.
Own the data ownership and accountability model: name Data Owners, Stewards, and Custodians, and hold them accountable through a defined sign-off cadence.
Deliver the enterprise business glossary under a tiered governance model, and maintain metadata management, lineage standards, and dbt metadata synchronization across the platform.
Set data quality thresholds and Trusted Layer certification criteria, and hold data observability (freshness, pipeline health, trust scores) to the same standard as financial controls.
Align controls as gates across the data delivery lifecycle (ingestion, definition, build, use, and govern), so a control fires wherever data advances and nothing reaches a certified output without passing.
Build data governance capability across the business through training and playbooks, rather than keeping expertise centralized.
Integration and Decision Authority
Act as the link between Business Controls and Data Governance called for in the integrated operating model: define control standards and evidence expectations alongside data definitions, and build controls into new systems and initiatives from the start.
Where control standards and data definitions conflict, collaborate with relevant stakeholders including, ED&A, Business Owners and Business Controls to resolve these inconsistencies. Work with ED&A / Technology and the Data Platform team so controls and governance are proactively built into the toolchain (Microsoft Fabric, dbt, Airflow, Power BI, Purview, Entra ID, Quadrant) by design.
Represent Data Governance in Risk & Integrated Assurance meetings and support Audit Committee reporting.
Team Leadership
Lead and develop direct report(s) and set clear deliverables and cadence for them..
Build team capability in data analytics, AI literacy, and integrated systems controls as the role grows, and build bench strength to move the environment from project to sustained run-state without single points of failure.
Build a “one team” culture between Business Controls and Data Governance that removes duplicate work and closes the gaps that used to sit between the two groups.

What Success Looks Like

Controls operating as gates, each with a named owner and re-performable evidence.
Audit outcomes: clean walkthroughs, deficiencies remediated, and SOC scope defensible.
Glossary and standards adopted, so certified numbers are built on agreed definitions.
Governance measured by delivery: trusted, in-use data products standing behind reported figures.
Direct reports delivering to plan, with growing capability and bench strength.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, Risk Management, Data Management, Computer Science, or a related discipline; Master is an asset.
8+ years of progressive experience across data governance, risk management, or audit, including at least 2 years leading people, and demonstrable end-to-end delivery of a control or governance environment.
Working knowledge of ICFR, SOC 1 / ISAE 3402, COSO 2013, ITGCs, and DAMA-DMBOK; CPA, CIA, CISA, or CDMP an asset. Familiarity with DCAM / CDMC and data contracts an asset.
Hands-on experience with data cataloguing and governance tooling (Microsoft Purview equivalents such as Collibra an asset) and with controls testing in an ICFR or SOX environment.
Working knowledge of a modern data-platform stack (Microsoft Fabric / lakehouse, dbt, Airflow, Power BI, Entra ID), enough to specify and validate controls.
Working knowledge of Yardi strongly preferred.
Investment and portfolio management literacy or business acumen
Proven ability to build controls that produce retained, re-testable evidence.
Ability to work across Finance, IT, and Data & Analytics, and turn technical and operational complexity into clear governance and control frameworks.
Comfortable preparing materials for senior leadership and the Audit Committee.
Comfortable building or growing an early-stage function.
Experience within real estate, asset management, pension, or investment management environments strongly preferred.

Purpose

As the Director of Commercial Pricing and Data Governance at UNFI, you are responsible for developing and executing the company's enterprise-wide pricing strategy while leading the Data Governance function. Your role is critical in driving commercial excellence, ensuring data integrity, and enabling informed business decisions across the organization.

In the area of pricing, your scope includes building and leading a centralized pricing department that will define, govern, and continuously improve UNFI Canada’s brand and customer pricing strategy. This role will move the organization toward a more disciplined pricing model, shifting pricing ownership away from Sales over time so that Sales can remain focused on customer relationships, execution of brand strategies, and commercial growth. You will immediately assume leadership of pricing activities currently managed within SRM and RGM, while developing the structure, tools, processes, resource requirements, governance model, and transition plan required to bring Sales pricing responsibilities into the pricing organization in the medium term. You will establish clear decision-making protocols, pricing guardrails, escalation processes, analytical capabilities, and best practices to support consistent, data-driven pricing decisions that improve margin performance, strengthen customer and supplier strategies, and deliver both immediate and long-term revenue value.

In the area of Data Governance, you will lead the Retalix Pricing, Retalix Maintenance, and MCB teams. You are accountable for ensuring data quality, governance, and integrity across Supplier Services, including pricing updates, GS1 data management, new brand onboarding information, and system master data maintenance. Your leadership will ensure that core data processes are effectively managed and aligned with business and operational requirements.

By partnering closely with cross-functional teams and senior leaders, you will enable the successful execution of UNFI's strategic priorities through the effective use of data and analytics. You will foster a culture of accountability, agility, and data-driven decision-making while ensuring alignment with UNFI's vision and objectives. Ultimately, your role is to drive sustainable revenue growth, improve profitability, and maximize the value of data as a strategic asset across the organization.

As Legal Counsel, you will serve as a key partner to the commercial legal team, providing privacy, data and cybersecurity subject matter expertise on complex commercial arrangements and supporting the development, review and negotiation of appropriate contractual protections.

What You'll Do

Champion privacy as a business enabler by driving stakeholder engagement and embedding privacy and data governance into products and services.

About Solink

At Solink, our mission is to safeguard what matters most
. We provide businesses with the tools to know sooner and act faster
by transforming video security into real-time operational insights.

Our cloud-based platform integrates seamlessly with your existing cameras and systems, turning them into intelligent sensors that detect and interpret key moments. This empowers teams to make data-driven decisions, enhance security, and improve operational efficiency.

Trusted by over 30,000 locations across 32+ countries - including brands like McDonald’s and JYSK - Solink delivers clarity when it counts. Our solutions help businesses reduce shrink, optimize performance, and respond proactively to potential threats.

We're growing rapidly, earning industry recognition, and scaling with purpose. We’ve been recognized by Deloitte’s Fast 50™ and Fast 500™, Business Intelligence Group, and as one of Ottawa’s Best Places to Work. And we’re just getting started!

The Role

Solink is at an inflection point in our growth journey. As Chief Financial Officer, you'll lead our financial strategy as we continue to scale and prepare the company for its next chapter of growth.

This is a critical leadership role, shaping both the day-to-day financial operations and the long-term strategic direction of the company. You'll bring a strong operational and strategic background, proven success scaling technology businesses, and the judgment to know when to zoom in on the details and when to zoom out to see the bigger picture.

What You'll Do

Lead the Finance Team: Oversee and develop the leaders of Solink’s FP&A and Accounting functions. Set clear priorities, strengthen collaboration between the teams, and hold them accountable for accurate, timely work and useful business insights.
Get Close to the Work: Understand how financial work gets done today, identify where processes break down, and work alongside the team to fix them. Bring the judgment and willingness to dig into details that a growing business needs.
Improve Processes and Systems: Simplify and document core finance processes, improve data quality, and introduce automation where it reduces manual work and errors. Build a function that can scale without relying on workarounds or individual heroics.
Strengthen Planning and Decision-Making: Guide the established FP&A function in delivering reliable budgets, forecasts, financial models, and analysis. Partner with leaders across Solink to turn that work into clear decisions and accountability for results.
Build Trust in Financial Reporting: Lead the Accounting function through a strong close, audit, and reporting cadence. Strengthen internal controls and ensure compliance with applicable GAAP/IFRS requirements while giving leaders confidence in the numbers.
Support Capital Strategy and Investor Relationships: Partner with the CEO and Board on financial strategy, capital needs, financing opportunities, and investor communications. Ensure Solink has the financial discipline and information needed to evaluate future opportunities.
Evaluate Strategic Opportunities: Assess potential acquisitions and partnerships, including due diligence, financial modelling, and the practical work required to integrate them successfully.

We are looking for an accomplished CPA who brings verifiable experience in high-growth software or technology-enabled companies—and the judgment, ownership, and execution skills to help build our next stage of growth.

Join us where excitement meets innovation and contribute to a world where trust and technology unite.

Employee Resource Groups: Belonging is an important part of doing your best work. Our ERGs provide an inclusive space, support and community for employees of diverse backgrounds and allies. We host informative, fun sessions and celebrations that are often open to the entire organization.

Position Summary

Trulioo is seeking a commercially minded and execution-oriented Senior Director, Global Privacy & Data Protection to lead our global privacy strategy, data protection program, and designated Data Protection Officer.

Reporting to the Chief Risk and Strategy Officer, this role will actively lead how privacy, data protection, AI governance, and responsible data use are embedded across Trulioo’s products, operations, commercial motions, and governed by leading practices. This is a senior leadership role for a privacy executive who can operate in scaling, agile environments and partnering with Product, Engineering, Legal, Security, Enterprise Risk, Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success.

The ideal candidate brings extensive expertise in GDPR, U.S. state privacy laws, and Canadian privacy laws, with experience in emerging areas including, but not limited to, biometrics, AI, age verification, data retention, data classification, and emerging identity technologies.

This role is expected to leverage AI and emerging technologies to improve productivity, enhance decision-making, and continuously optimize how work is performed.

This will be a full-time, permanent position working on a hybrid model from one of our North American offices or fully remote.

What You’ll Be Doing

Global Privacy Strategy & DPO

Build and lead Trulioo’s global privacy and data protection strategy across priority markets, products, customers, and operating environments.
Serve as Trulioo’s designated Data Protection Officer for Europe, providing independent, credible, and commercially practical advice on GDPR and related obligations.
Advise executive leadership, as needed, on privacy risk, regulatory change, customer expectations, and strategic trade-offs tied to product innovation and market expansion.
Represent Trulioo in privacy-related engagements with regulators, enterprise customers, industry groups, and other external stakeholders.
Act as a strategic advisor on privacy and data protection implications as Trulioo expands into new operating regions, verticals, and expands the product catalog.
Monitor global privacy developments and translate implications into practical guidance for products, operations, market expansion, and customer commitments.

Privacy Program Operations & Governance

Mature Trulioo’s privacy program, including PIAs, DPIAs, records of processing, data subject rights, vendor privacy reviews, and cross-border transfer mechanisms. Integrate privacy by design into product development, commercial contracting, customer onboarding, third-party management, enterprise risk management, and agile operating rhythms.

jobs.title: Sr. Director, AI Architect
jobs.description:
About Patra

Patra is an outcome-focused operating partner working exclusively for the insurance industry. Combining expert global teams, process intelligence, and purpose-built technology, Patra delivers measurable results to clients. With 20 years of deep domain expertise, exceptional client retention rates, and significant sustained investment in AI, Patra partners with agencies, brokers, MGAs, MGUs, and carriers to transform how insurance operations are delivered.

Core Duties

AI and data are becoming foundational capabilities across Patra’s technology organization. The AI & Data Architecture function establishes the enterprise architecture, platforms, governance, and shared capabilities that enable product teams to build intelligent applications safely and at scale.

As AI Architect, you will lead Patra’s AI & Data Architecture function, operating at a Sr. Director-level scope with responsibility for its strategy, team formation and management, systems architecture, strategic priorities, and, most importantly, reliable and impactful execution.

The function has particular responsibility for document-intensive and unstructured-data environments, including retrieval-augmented generation, semantic and vector search, AI agents, evaluation datasets, enterprise analytics, and granular AI observability.

You will report to the Chief Digital Officer (CDO) and partner with senior leaders across Engineering, Product, Security, Compliance, Business Intelligence, Operations, and other business functions.

What you'll do

Lead the AI & Data Architecture function. Own the strategy, organizational structure, technical direction, priorities, delivery, quality, and operating model for Patra’s enterprise AI and data capabilities.
Form and lead the organization. Determine staffing requirements and build multidisciplinary teams spanning AI engineering, data engineering, machine learning, enterprise data architecture, analytics infrastructure, and shared AI services, while personally delivering on urgent business priorities at the same time
Manage talent and performance. Establish objectives for direct reports as your team grows, evaluate performance, provide career and leadership development, and exercise delegated authority to make or recommend decisions concerning hiring, promotions, compensation, organizational assignments, and other personnel actions.
Own the enterprise AI and data architecture. Establish Patra’s target-state architecture for how data is ingested, governed, modeled, stored, streamed, retrieved, analyzed, and consumed by enterprise applications, analytics platforms, and AI systems.
Direct architecture for document-intensive and unstructured domains. Establish enterprise standards and approve architectural approaches for document ingestion,

metadata extraction, indexing, semantic retrieval, vector search, knowledge enrichment, and AI consumption. Detailed design and implementation are delegated to subordinate professional teams.

Industrialize the Agentic AI platform. Direct the evolution of agentic capabilities into production-grade enterprise infrastructure supporting agent orchestration, tool integration, retrieval-augmented generation, model interaction, security boundaries, evaluation, observability, and appropriate human oversight.
Own AI evaluation and data strategy. Establish the standards and organizational processes governing training, fine-tuning, benchmarking, and evaluation datasets, including quality, provenance, versioning, access, retention, and appropriate use.
Treat AI observability as a strategic data asset. Establish the architecture and governance for capturing and using event streams across agent activity, model interactions, retrieval operations, tool execution, quality signals, latency, cost, failures, and human interventions.
Lead the enterprise data platform strategy. Set direction for cloud-native data capabilities including AWS services such as S3, Redshift, streaming and event technologies, together with platforms such as Snowflake and/or Databricks where appropriate.
Establish enterprise data standards. Define and govern modern approaches to operational, analytical, event-driven, semantic, and AI-oriented data modeling and ensure common architectural standards are adopted across engineering teams.
Make Business Intelligence a first-class platform stakeholder. Ensure enterprise data capabilities support analytics, operational reporting, experimentation, decision support, and executive intelligence without relying on fragmented downstream data extraction.
Build governance into the architecture. Establish standards for data ownership, lineage, provenance, classification, quality, lifecycle management, access control, AI usage, auditability, and enterprise data governance.
Protect customer and tenant data. Establish architecture and controls for strict multi-tenant client-data segregation across storage, processing, analytics, retrieval, model interaction, evaluation, and observability systems.
Own jurisdiction-aware data architecture. Establish retention, archival, residency, and deletion strategies supporting differing contractual, regulatory, and jurisdictional requirements.
Set quality and reliability expectations. Establish SLAs, SLOs, quality metrics, and operational standards for critical data assets, pipelines, AI services, retrieval systems, and shared platform capabilities.
Establish reusable platform capabilities. Direct the development of common capabilities for identity, access, observability, model access, AI evaluation, security, compliance controls, tenancy, CI/CD, and data services that can be consumed across product organizations.
Direct enterprise integration architecture. Establish standards for integrating AI and data platforms with Patra products, internal business systems, partner platforms, APIs, event streams, and external data providers.
Run AI and data capabilities as enterprise products. Treat product engineers, analytics teams, business stakeholders, and other internal organizations as customers of the platform. Establish adoption, reliability, quality, and developer-productivity measures for shared capabilities.
Own architecture governance. Lead reviews of material AI, data, and platform architecture decisions; establish reference architectures and engineering standards; approve significant architectural approaches; and resolve cross-organizational technical decisions.
Direct the AI and data portfolio. Establish priorities across concurrent AI, data, and platform programs and allocate engineering and data-science resources according to business value, organizational capacity, technical dependencies, and enterprise risk.
Manage technology investment. Participate in annual planning, determine staffing and platform requirements, develop budget recommendations, evaluate strategic technology vendors, and make or recommend investment decisions involving AI, cloud, data, and infrastructure platforms.
Shape the multi-year technology roadmap. Partner with executive engineering and product leadership to define Patra’s AI and data roadmap and translate strategic objectives into sequenced, staffed, and measurable organizational programs.
Represent the function with senior leadership. Advise executives on AI strategy, enterprise data architecture, platform investments, organizational capacity, delivery risk, AI risk, governance, and major technology trade-offs.

How You Think About AI And Data Platforms

We are looking for a leader whose operating instincts align with how we build.

Build shared capabilities once. Identity, observability, model access, evaluation, security, governance, tenancy, CI/CD, and data access should be established as reusable platform capabilities rather than repeatedly implemented by individual teams.
Data is a product. Enterprise data, documents, application events, model interactions, evaluation results, and observability signals are strategic assets with defined owners, contracts, quality expectations, governance, and consumers.
AI-ready from ingestion onward. Documents, metadata, events, permissions, lineage, and semantic context should be designed so that they can safely support applications, analytics, machine learning, retrieval, and agentic systems.
Governance is architecture. Customer isolation, security, retention, residency, auditability, Responsible AI, and regulatory considerations are architectural requirements rather than controls added after systems have been built.
Evaluation precedes confidence. Production AI requires measurable success criteria, curated evaluation datasets, regression testing, observability, and mechanisms for detecting degraded behavior.
Observability is a first-class data asset. Agent activity, retrievals, model calls, tool calls, cost, latency, failures, quality signals, user feedback, and human interventions should produce structured and governed telemetry.
Automation over operational heroics. Repeated manual intervention represents an architectural or platform gap. Provisioning, deployment, evaluation, governance checks, and operational processes should increasingly be automated.
Self-service over central bottlenecks. The AI & Data Architecture organization exists to increase the leverage of engineering and product teams, not to become a ticket queue they must pass through.
Human oversight is intentional. Increasing autonomy should be accompanied by explicit decision boundaries, escalation mechanisms, auditability, and controls appropriate to the risk of the workflow.
Incremental over big-bang. Major platform transitions should produce measurable production value incrementally, with explicit migration plans and accountable milestones.
Specifications precede implementation. As AI accelerates implementation, clear requirements, contracts, architectural boundaries, evaluation criteria, and ownership become more important.
Decisions are explicit. Make trade-offs visible across cost, risk, reliability, security, scalability, and time-to-value. Once a decision is made, establish ownership and execute against it.

Qualifications

Technical and organizational depth. 10+ years of progressive experience across software engineering, enterprise architecture, data engineering, cloud platforms, artificial intelligence, or machine learning, including significant experience leading senior technical professionals.
Organizational leadership. Demonstrated experience forming, scaling, and leading multidisciplinary engineering and data organizations.
People management. Experience hiring professional employees, developing managers and technical leaders, evaluating performance, making promotion and compensation recommendations, planning organizational capacity, and allocating resources across teams and strategic initiatives.
Enterprise AI credibility. Deep understanding of production AI systems including LLM applications, RAG, embeddings, semantic and vector search, agentic architectures, AI orchestration, evaluation, observability, governance, and human-in-the-loop systems.
Enterprise data architecture. Significant experience directing the architecture of platforms supporting structured, semi-structured, and unstructured enterprise data.
Document-intensive domains. Experience with architectures where documents and unstructured information are important business assets supporting operational workflows, search, analytics, AI, and governance.
Cloud and modern data platforms. Experience establishing strategy around AWS-native data services including S3, Redshift, streaming and event technologies, as well as platforms such as Snowflake and/or Databricks.
Modern data architecture. Strong understanding of operational, analytical, dimensional, event-oriented, lakehouse, semantic, and domain-oriented data architectures and their trade-offs.

Who are we?

Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.

A place where bold ideas are welcomed, human connection is valued, and everyone has the opportunity to shape their future.

A career at Equinix means being at the center of shaping what comes next and amplifying customer value through innovation and impact. You’ll work across teams, influence key decisions, and help shape the path forward. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work.

Job Summary

Serve as a strategic advisor and execution partner to the Chief AI Officer, helping shape and deliver Equinix’s enterprise AI agenda. The role spans AI strategy and governance, enterprise adoption and value realization, organizational capability, and the external AI ecosystem. Translate priorities into funded plans and measurable outcomes, strengthen executive decision-making, and enable the AI leadership team to operate effectively across a global organization.

The successful candidate combines independent judgment, practical AI fluency, and hands-on execution. They anticipate what needs attention, challenge assumptions constructively, and take ownership of complex work from initial framing through completion.

Responsibilities

Strategic Planning & Executive Advisory

Partner with the CAIO to define and communicate the enterprise AI strategy, priorities, and investment roadmap, connecting internal transformation with Equinix’s broader AI business and ecosystem strategy
Develop decision briefs with clear recommendations, alternatives, financial implications, and risks. Provide candid advice and test the assumptions behind major proposals
Assess emerging AI capabilities, competitors, and partnerships, distinguishing developments that warrant action from those that warrant monitoring
Lead strategic initiatives and special projects from problem definition through delivery, establishing ownership and transitioning ongoing responsibilities to the appropriate teams

Business Operations & Execution

Own the AI leadership team’s operating rhythm, including planning, portfolio reviews, leadership meetings, and offsites. Structure forums around decisions, with clear owners, deadlines, and follow-through
Drive portfolio visibility across priorities, dependencies, investment, and results. Work with Finance and business owners to validate value assumptions and distinguish realized benefits from forecasts
Coordinate budget and workforce planning with Finance and HR. Surface resource trade-offs and recommend where to accelerate, adjust, or stop investment
Resolve execution barriers with accountable leaders and escalate material risks early, with options and a recommended course of action
Represent the CAIO as delegated, exercising judgment within agreed decision rights and keeping the CAIO informed of consequential commitments

Cross-Functional Alignment & Stakeholder Engagement

Build trusted partnerships with executive leaders, Chiefs of Staff, and business owners to secure sponsorship and drive enterprise AI adoption and value realization
Resolve cross-functional dependencies and competing priorities. Make ownership explicit and address difficult issues directly and constructively
Lead preparation of Board and executive materials, decision memos, and organizational communications, translating technical detail into clear business implications and specific asks
Prepare the CAIO for customer, partner, and industry engagements. Define the purpose of each engagement and drive follow-through, aligning external messaging with Communications and Marketing

Organizational Effectiveness & Transformation

Partner with the AI leadership team and HR on operating model evolution, workforce priorities, and leadership development. Identify capability gaps and clarify responsibilities as the organization scales
Coordinate with AI governance, Security, Legal, and other control functions to bring responsible AI requirements and unresolved risk decisions into portfolio planning and executive reviews
Advance AI fluency and change initiatives with business leaders, using adoption and outcome evidence to identify what needs to change
Improve how the organization works through simple processes and practical use of AI, reducing manual reporting and unnecessary meetings. Model a culture of High Standard, Low Bureaucracy, Zero Blame

Qualifications

Knowledge & Experience

10+ years of experience in strategy, business operations, consulting, Chief of Staff, product, data, AI, or related leadership roles, with demonstrated ownership of execution and business results
Strong understanding of enterprise AI and technology operating models, including generative AI, agents, shared platforms, adoption barriers, and AI economics and risk. Able to engage credibly with technical and business leaders
Proven experience delivering complex initiatives across a large, global, matrixed organization, including resolving competing priorities and recovering work that is off track
Strong financial and analytical acumen, with experience in business cases, investment prioritization, budget planning, and benefits measurement
Experience personally developing executive communications, Board materials, and strategic plans that require limited revision and support consequential decisions
Experience partnering with C-suite executives through ambiguity and organizational change. Prior Chief of Staff experience is valuable; equivalent operating leadership experience is equally relevant

Skills & Attributes

Strategic judgment: Frame the right problem, make trade-offs, and offer an independent point of view
Execution discipline: Take ownership without waiting for detailed direction and close commitments reliably
Executive communication: Synthesize complex issues into concise, accurate writing and clear discussion
Trust and discretion: Handle sensitive matters with integrity and the confidence to challenge respectfully
Influence and collaboration: Build credibility across functions and hold peers accountable while preserving trust
Learning agility: Develop technical and business context quickly, use AI tools effectively, and verify their outputs
Calm leadership: Remain effective under pressure, recognize when to act independently and when to escalate, and put team outcomes first

jobs.description:
Machine Learning Engineer, Associate Director – AI Innovation Teams

Fitch Ratings is seeking a Machine Learning Engineer to join our new AI Innovation teams in Toronto—a bold initiative building the AI-powered future of financial analysis. We're not fine-tuning existing models or optimizing yesterday's algorithms. We're architecting the next generation: sophisticated agentic AI systems, intelligent automation that thinks, and ML capabilities that will redefine how credit analysis happens and how global financial markets consume insights.

This is AI's moment at Fitch, and we're moving decisively. We have executive sponsorship, significant investment, and we're establishing Toronto as our AI innovation center. As a Lead ML Engineer, you'll be a technical champion driving this transformation—building breakthrough ML systems that others will study, mentoring engineers who will become tomorrow's AI leaders, and establishing patterns that will scale across the organization. You're joining at the perfect inflection point: early enough to architect foundational decisions, resourced enough to execute boldly.

We need ML technologists who see greenfield opportunities as fuel rather than fear—whether you're an ML architect ready to design intelligent systems from first principles, an AI engineering leader who translates research breakthroughs into production reality, or a seasoned practitioner who recognizes that this moment demands courage over caution. If you're motivated by "let's prove this is possible" rather than "we need more data before we decide," this is a high-impact role where you'll spend less time justifying AI's potential and more time realizing it—alongside exceptional engineers who share your conviction that we're building something significant.

This role is ideal for someone who wants to remain deeply hands-on while operating at a senior level. You will contribute technical expertise, influence decision-making through strong engineering judgment, and partner closely with engineering leaders, product teams, and fellow engineers to deliver innovative AI solutions at scale. This is a senior individual contributor role with no direct people management responsibilities

What We Offer

Ground-floor ML leadership with enterprise resources – Define the ML architecture, technical standards, and engineering practices for Fitch's AI future while having the compute, research budgets, and organizational backing that most AI startups would envy; mentor and coach fellow ML engineers while remaining deeply hands-on with the most challenging technical problems
Build breakthrough ML systems that matter – Develop net-new generative AI platforms, multi-agent orchestration systems, and intelligent automation that will process billions in credit decisions; experiment with frontier models, novel architectures, and unconventional approaches; see your ML innovations directly impact how global financial markets operate
Access to cutting-edge ML infrastructure and research – Work with the latest LLMs, fine-tune foundation models, leverage enterprise-scale GPU clusters, experiment with emerging frameworks before they're mainstream, and collaborate with academic ML researchers; substantial conference and training budgets to stay at the forefront of AI innovation
Toronto as Fitch's AI center of excellence – Join our strategic investment in Toronto—one of the world's premier AI research hubs—where you'll connect with Vector Institute researchers, attend cutting-edge ML meetups, and be part of the ecosystem that's defining the future of applied AI
Shape ML governance and standards for an organization – Establish the ML engineering practices, model governance frameworks, and AI integration patterns that will guide Fitch's AI transformation; your architectural decisions will influence how a global financial services leader approaches intelligent systems
Real production impact with sophisticated ML challenges – Build ML systems that analysts and financial professionals actually use daily; solve hard problems at the intersection of NLP, document intelligence, reasoning systems, and production-scale deployment; measure your impact in both model performance and business outcomes
Accelerated career trajectory in AI leadership – High visibility to C-suite executives making billion-dollar strategic decisions; clear advancement paths to Principal ML Architect or AI Research Lead roles; opportunity to establish yourself as a recognized voice in financial AI and earn a reputation that opens doors across the industry

We'll Count On You To

Build transformative ML systems from the ground up – Design and architect net-new generative AI solutions, agentic workflows, and intelligent platforms using advanced ML frameworks (PyTorch, etc.), large language models, and emerging AI technologies that fundamentally change how analysts work and how Fitch operates
Drive breakthrough AI innovation and experimentation boldly – Lead exploration of generative AI, multi-agent systems, RAG architectures, model fine-tuning, prompt engineering, and other emerging ML technologies; create cutting-edge proofs-of-concept; evaluate what's transformative versus what's hype; and turn research into production-quality AI capabilities

Deep ML technical expertise – 12+ years of professional experience building production AI/ML systems, with strong proficiency in Python, ML algorithms (from classical techniques to deep learning), and modern ML frameworks; proven track record of delivering advanced generative AI and ML solutions

Technical leadership and influence – Track record of mentoring and coaching engineers, driving ML initiatives in fast-moving environments, leading through technical excellence and influence rather than authority, and building credibility through results and vision

What Would Make You Stand Out

Cutting-edge AI research to production experience – Track record of taking breakthrough AI capabilities from research/prototype to production-scale deployment; experience supporting seamless transitions from experimentation to enterprise-grade ML systems with real users
ML thought leadership and technical strategy – History of establishing technical direction for ML initiatives, contributing to open-source ML projects, speaking at AI/ML conferences, publishing research, or writing about practical applications of emerging AI technologies

jobs.title: Director, Intelligent Enterprise Transformation Leader - Finance
jobs.description:
We are the leading provider of professional services to the middle market globally, our purpose is to instill confidence in a world of change, empowering our clients and people to realize their full potential. Our exceptional people are the key to our unrivaled, inclusive culture and talent experience and our ability to be compelling to our clients. You’ll find an environment that inspires and empowers you to thrive both personally and professionally. There’s no one like you and that’s why there’s nowhere like RSM.

RSM Consulting is seeking a Director to serve as Business Transformation Lead on large, integrated Intelligent Finance transformations. Our Intelligent Finance portfolio helps clients build the intelligent foundation and activate AI for Finance at scale — spanning ERP Modernization, Finance Operating Model Transformations, Finance Data & Analytics Modernization and AI Readiness, AI Enablement & Agentic Automation for the Office of Finance as well as Finance Service Delivery Transformations – including centralization, Finance Shared Services and Global Finance Service Delivery.

This is the pivotal business-side leadership role on the transformation. You own how the client operates differently once the platform is live. You are not the program manager and you are not the solution architect — you are the leader accountable for the future-state operating model, the end-to-end processes, the human experience of the change, and the executive confidence that the business, not just the technology, actually changed. Your success is measured by a single question: did the business change successfully?

You will be dedicated to one major transformation at a time, working as a peer alongside the Executive Transformation Partner, the Transformation Director, and the Platform & Delivery Lead.

Responsibilities

Operating Model and Process Ownership
Own the design and operationalization of the future-state operating model for the Finance and Operations functions — finance, supply chain, service, IT, and the shared data and reporting layer that the modernized core creates.
Lead end-to-end business capability and process design across core cycles affected by ERP, Finance point solutions, cloud, data, and AI enablement work, and define how those processes operate in a modernized, increasingly automated environment.
Define the organization, role, skill, decision-rights, and control implications of a modern core and an agentic operating environment — including which decisions become automated, which remain human, and how exceptions are handled and governed.
Establish how data ownership, stewardship, and definitional consistency are carried by the business after the build team leaves.
Maintain traceability from the client’s business case through operating-model changes, process changes, backlog priorities, adoption outcomes, and value delivered.

Human-Centered Design

Own Human-Centered Design as a funded, staffed, and measured workstream from mobilization — not a go-live activity.
Start from user jobs-to-be-done for Finance, rather than screens; ensure personas and journey maps for finance, operations, and service users drive requirements before build.
Prototype and test with real users ahead of build, and use “art-of-the-possible” demonstrations of modern and AI-enabled capability to build executive and user confidence early.
Ensure HCD findings materially shape scope — including where an AI or automation use case is not yet appropriate for the client’s data maturity or risk tolerance.

Organizational Change Management and Adoption

Own OCM as a funded, measured workstream: leader alignment and visible sponsorship from day one, stakeholder analysis, communications, resistance management, role-based training, and readiness scoring.
Baseline adoption targets and tie them explicitly to benefits realization — system usage, process compliance, automation acceptance rates, exception volumes, and reporting adoption.
Lead the business through the behavioral shift that modernization demands: fewer manual reconciliations, more trust in a single data source, and confident supervision of automated and agent-assisted work.

Backlog, Value Mapping and Delivery Cadence

Lead weekly backlog refinement and own product backlog integrity and value mapping — from business drivers through requirements, capabilities, features, adoption outcomes, and measurable benefits.
Participate in each sprint’s feature review and system demonstration alongside the client Product Owner and the Platform & Delivery Lead, assessing whether what was built changes how the business actually works.
Participate in increment planning and Inspect & Adapt retrospectives, testing outcomes against the client’s original drivers.
Ensure outcome milestones are tracked alongside technical and delivery milestones.

Transformation Leadership and Client Confidence

Serve as the bridge between technical delivery and executive confidence, presenting evidence of business change to sponsors, steering committees, and the Executive Risk Committee.
Escalate early, with a recommended action rather than a status — particularly on scope that risks delivering a platform without an operating-model change.
Plan for complexity: competing stakeholder demands, third-party and systems-integrator friction, legacy-process attachment, and key-person risk on both sides.
Bring in-person presence to large or sensitive transformations.

Practice and People Leadership

Contribute to the growth of RSM’s Total Consulting transformation capability, including methods, tools, and reusable intellectual property for operating-model design, HCD, and adoption measurement.
Mentor, coach, and develop managers and senior associates across HCD, process design, and change workstreams
Support pursuits, proposals, and thought leadership that position RSM as a leader in integrated, outcome-led modernization; help shape scope, approach, and change-workstream sizing before mobilization.
Support account expansion through demonstrated value, and maintain strong attention to engagement economics within your workstreams.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree.
10+ years of consulting or advisory experience, including significant experience leading business-side transformation on large enterprise technology programs.
Demonstrated ownership of the Finance future-state operating model and end-to-end process design on ERP, cloud, data, or AI-enabled programs.
Demonstrated ownership of change and adoption as a funded workstream, including baselined adoption targets tied to benefits.
Experience operating in a fixed Agile or scaled-Agile cadence, including product backlog ownership, backlog refinement, and sprint demonstrations with an active client Product Owner.
Strong executive presence and the ability to hold candid, evidence-based conversations with C-suite sponsors.
Practical understanding of modern ERP, cloud, data, and AI platform capability — sufficient to shape requirements and challenge design, without acting as the technical architect.
Commitment to responsible AI use with a human in the loop and human accountability for all client-facing judgments and outputs.
Willingness and ability to travel as needed, generally up to 50%, with in-person presence on large programs.

Preferred Qualifications

CPA and / or Masters in Business Administration, with a focus on Accounting, Finance or Operations
Experience on transformations where an implementation was deliberately converted into a program as scope expanded across process, organization, and adoption.
Experience designing operating models for finance, supply chain, or shared-services functions in a modernized core environment.
Experience establishing AI and automation governance from a business-process and control perspective.
Change certification such as Prosci/ADKAR; design-thinking or service-design credentials; SAFe Agilist, PMI-ACP, or Scrum Master certification

At RSM, we offer a competitive benefits and compensation package for all our people. Learn more about our total rewards at https://rsmcanada.com/careers/life-at-rsm/rewards-and-benefits.html.

We believe flexibility and in-person connection both play an important role in how we work and grow. Most roles at RSM follow a hybrid workstyle, which means team members are aligned to an RSM office and come together in person when it best supports clients, teams, development or relationship-building. At Seneca Polytechnic, we offer a flexible working environment that supports innovative thinking and encourages exploring new ideas and approaches. Are you a technology leader who can simplify complexity?

At Seneca Polytechnic, technology powers every aspect of the student, employee, and academic experience. As Seneca continues to strengthen its leadership in artificial intelligence within the postsecondary sector, we are investing in modern enterprise applications, cloud platforms, data capabilities and AI-enabled solutions that support teaching, learning and institutional operations. We are looking for a technology leader who can navigate complex enterprise environments, build trusted partnerships and deliver practical, scalable solutions that advance Seneca's strategic priorities.

Reporting to the CIO, the Director, Enterprise Software Solutions leads the teams responsible for enterprise applications, systems integration, business intelligence, application development and production support. You will shape Seneca’s information solutions strategy, modernize its digital environment and help ensure technology investments improve teaching, learning, institutional services and student success.

Work with academic and administrative leaders to understand the real business problem, clarify essential requirements and design solutions that fit Seneca’s needs, resources and budget.

Oversee a complex portfolio of more than 100 enterprise and custom applications, including student, learning, CRM, finance, human resources, analytics, cloud and AI solutions, while working directly with major technology providers and maximizing internal capability.

Position: Chief Financial Officer

Status: Permanent, full time
Salary Range: From $250,000 + incentive pay
Location:
Whitehorse, Yukon or remote with monthly onsite presence

The opportunity

Northern Vision Development is growing. For more than two decades, NVD has built and operated hotels, restaurants, commercial and residential real estate, seniors living, and development assets across Yukon and British Columbia.

As Chief Financial Officer, you will shape how NVD grows, allocates capital, manages risk, and creates long-term value for its unitholders and communities. The decisions ahead about where to invest, how to finance it and how much risk to carry will shape the company for decades to come. This is an opportunity to bring Drive to an ambitious growth agenda, Rigour to complex financial decisions, and Kindness to the relationships and leadership required to move the organization forward.

What does your success look like?

The CEO and Board rely on your advice for major investment, development and financing decisions, and those decisions rest on tested assumptions and clear expectations for return and risk.
NVD can see ahead on liquidity, capital capacity, and covenant headroom, and grow without putting its financial resilience or lender relationships at risk.
The Board, Audit Committee, unitholders, and lenders trust NVD’s financial reporting because it is timely, dependable, and useful for decisions.
Operating leaders use forecasts and performance information to make decisions and are accountable for their results.
NVD has a clear, well-reasoned decision on the direction of its financial systems.
Partnership and ownership structures with First Nation partners are financially sound and clearly understood by all parties.
The finance function has leadership, structure, and capability the business needs, and its people grow under your leadership.

IMMEDIATE INTERIM OPPORTUNITY

Interim Vice President, Finance & Facilities

Reports to EVP Corporate Services

100% virtual

12-15 month engagement

Our client is a highly reputable Canadian organization
with a significant and multifaceted mandate. During a period of leadership transition, they are seeking an accomplished Interim Vice President, Finance & Facilities
to provide stability, strong financial stewardship and experienced leadership while helping position the organization for its next chapter.

This is more than a maintenance assignment. It is an opportunity for an experienced finance executive to come in, make an immediate impact and elevate an already high-performing function
. The successful interim will inherit a capable team and will be expected to provide visible leadership, bring fresh perspective, strengthen financial insight and discipline, and identify opportunities to enhance the sophistication and effectiveness of the function.
The mandate spans financial reporting, planning, performance management, risk and controls, treasury, facilities and procurement, while providing senior leadership with thoughtful financial advice and insight.

The Mandate

Working closely with the senior executive team, the Interim VP will take leadership of the finance function and ensure continued strength in the organization's financial management during the transition.

This is a role for someone equally comfortable around the executive table and in the details
. The successful executive will be strategic when the situation requires it, but willing to roll up their sleeves, challenge assumptions, solve problems and help the team execute.

Key priorities will include:

Providing strong financial stewardship
, ensuring the continued integrity, accuracy and timeliness of financial reporting, forecasting and financial operations.
Leading and supporting a strong finance team, creating clarity, engagement and momentum through a period of change.
Acting as a trusted financial advisor to senior leadership, bringing insight to organizational performance, longer-term planning and decision-making.
Reviewing existing financial processes, controls and practices and identifying opportunities to modernize, streamline and elevate the sophistication of the function.
Providing leadership across facilities management and procurement, ensuring strong governance, commercial discipline and effective execution.
Strengthening budgeting, forecasting, cash-flow planning, risk management and performance reporting.
Working effectively with external advisors, auditors and other key stakeholders.
Supporting senior leadership and the organization's governance bodies with credible, thoughtful financial insight. The underlying position specifically supports Audit and Finance Committee and Board activities.
Looking beyond business-as-usual to identify opportunities to drive change, improve effectiveness and leave the organization stronger at the conclusion of the mandate.

The Ideal Interim Executive

We are looking for a seasoned financial executive who knows how to enter an established organization, quickly understand the environment and add value without unnecessary disruption
.

Ideally, this individual will bring a combination of not-for-profit and commercial experience
, pairing an understanding of stewardship, governance and stakeholder accountability with the commercial instincts and operational discipline of the private sector.

The ideal candidate will bring:

Significant senior financial leadership experience within a complex organization.
A professional accounting designation, with strong technical grounding across accounting, financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting and internal controls. The underlying profile calls for a CPA/CA-preferred designation and experience with IFRS, ASPE and ASNPO.
Experience leading strong teams through periods of transition, change or transformation
.
A genuinely hands-on style. Someone prepared to get into the numbers and issues rather than lead exclusively from 30,000 feet.
The ability to move comfortably between strategy and execution
.
Exposure to facilities, procurement and broader corporate services would be highly valuable.
Strong executive presence and the ability to establish credibility quickly with senior executives, employees, external advisors and governance stakeholders.
A pragmatic, collaborative leadership style with the confidence to respectfully challenge the status quo.
Experience operating across both mission-driven/not-for-profit and commercially oriented environments
would be particularly attractive.

Why This Assignment?

For the right interim executive, this offers the opportunity to do what great interims do best: step into an important organization at an important moment and make a measurable difference.

You will be joining a high-performing team rather than rebuilding a broken function. The opportunity is to provide leadership through transition, bring an objective external lens, elevate financial and operational practices, and create sustainable improvements that remain long after the assignment has concluded.

THE OPPORTUNITY

We have an exceptional opportunity for a strategic, government-savvy finance leader to serve as Director of Finance and help shape the fiscal future of the Town of High Level. Reporting to the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO), the Director of Finance is responsible for the overall leadership and management of the Town’s financial operations. This includes overseeing strategic financial planning, accounting, revenue collection, and cash management, ensuring alignment with the Town’s adopted plans, policies, bylaws, regulations, and standards. In addition to fostering interdepartmental collaboration and ensuring compliance with all financial obligations as outlined in the Municipal Government Act (MGA), the Director supervises a team of four (4): a Financial Analyst, Accounts Payable and Receivable Clerk, Utilities and Tax Clerk, and Support Services Clerk.

THE ORGANIZATION

The Town of High Level is a vibrant northern community of approximately 4,000 residents, serving as the regional service and trading centre for a surrounding population of more than 30,000 people. Located in the northwest corner of Alberta, High Level is strategically positioned at the intersection of Highways 35 and 58, providing critical access to northern industries and communities.

High Level is recognized as a hub for healthcare, education, retail, construction, transportation, and resource development, offering a unique blend of professional challenge and community connection. Known for its breathtaking Northern Lights, endless summer days and access to pristine lakes, rivers and outdoor adventures, the Town is a gateway to exceptional northern living. Residents also enjoy a strong sense of community and rich Indigenous culture, with local festivals, rodeos, and family-oriented activities year-round.

Vision

High Level, an inclusive and vibrant community, with a strong and resilient economy that offers an active and healthy lifestyle.

Mission

We foster a thriving community that enhances our quality of life through sustainable planning, economic prosperity, and inclusion.

For more information, please visit their website: www.highlevel.ca

RESPONSIBILITIES

Plans, directs and coordinates the functions and workload within the Department and ensures that schedules, procedures and performance standards are developed and met.
Utilizes significant judgement, initiative and conceptual thinking in the planning, development and implementation of programs and policies affecting matters related to the scope of duties of this position.
Plans, directs and coordinates the preparation of annual and long-term operational and capital budgets. Provides direct oversight, control and implementation of approved budgets.
Responsible for the preparation of statements and reports on municipal financial affairs for CAO, Directors, Council and the public; includes financial reports on the status and variance of all operating and capital budgets.
Responsible for compiling and supplying information relating to the financial affairs of the municipality as required by Municipal Affairs.
Prepares all financial bylaws, resolutions and subsequent amendments relating to the revenues, expenditures, tax levies and other fiscal and operating matters within the scope of duties of this position. Supports procurement and contract management processes to ensure fiscal responsibility.
Oversees the development and maintenance of the Town’s asset management plan, including strategies, policies and procedures.
Oversees the development of policies for Financial Services. Provides input to policies of other departments.
Provides advice to Town staff, including explanation and interpretation of bylaws, procedures and legislative requirements affecting the Financial Administration department related to the scope of duties of this position.
Responsible for the supervision and mentoring of finance staff including hiring, training, dismissal, appraisals and evaluations of Financial Services employees within approved personnel policies.
Directs, coordinates, and supervises subordinate staff activities and contract staff. Monitors their work performance and delegates work appropriately.
Prepares, or directs the preparation, of reports and makes recommendations to the Chief Administrative Officer on financial matters related to the scope of duties of the position.
Attends all Council meetings, Committee meetings, public hearings and public meetings as required and as directed by the Chief Administrative Officer.
Prepares reports and statistical summaries as necessary for review by the Chief Administrative Officer, Council or other bodies.
As a member of the Senior Management Team, supports and assists other senior managers and is respectful of colleagues' roles, responsibilities and perspectives.

new_jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer, Associate Director
new_jobs.description:
Machine Learning Engineer, Associate Director – AI Innovation Teams

Fitch Ratings is seeking a Machine Learning Engineer to join our new AI Innovation teams in Toronto—a bold initiative building the AI-powered future of financial analysis. We're not fine-tuning existing models or optimizing yesterday's algorithms. We're architecting the next generation: sophisticated agentic AI systems, intelligent automation that thinks, and ML capabilities that will redefine how credit analysis happens and how global financial markets consume insights.

This is AI's moment at Fitch, and we're moving decisively. We have executive sponsorship, significant investment, and we're establishing Toronto as our AI innovation center. As a Lead ML Engineer, you'll be a technical champion driving this transformation—building breakthrough ML systems that others will study, mentoring engineers who will become tomorrow's AI leaders, and establishing patterns that will scale across the organization. You're joining at the perfect inflection point: early enough to architect foundational decisions, resourced enough to execute boldly.

We need ML technologists who see greenfield opportunities as fuel rather than fear—whether you're an ML architect ready to design intelligent systems from first principles, an AI engineering leader who translates research breakthroughs into production reality, or a seasoned practitioner who recognizes that this moment demands courage over caution. If you're motivated by "let's prove this is possible" rather than "we need more data before we decide," this is a high-impact role where you'll spend less time justifying AI's potential and more time realizing it—alongside exceptional engineers who share your conviction that we're building something significant.

This role is ideal for someone who wants to remain deeply hands-on while operating at a senior level. You will contribute technical expertise, influence decision-making through strong engineering judgment, and partner closely with engineering leaders, product teams, and fellow engineers to deliver innovative AI solutions at scale. This is a senior individual contributor role with no direct people management responsibilities

What We Offer

Ground-floor ML leadership with enterprise resources – Define the ML architecture, technical standards, and engineering practices for Fitch's AI future while having the compute, research budgets, and organizational backing that most AI startups would envy; mentor and coach fellow ML engineers while remaining deeply hands-on with the most challenging technical problems
Build breakthrough ML systems that matter – Develop net-new generative AI platforms, multi-agent orchestration systems, and intelligent automation that will process billions in credit decisions; experiment with frontier models, novel architectures, and unconventional approaches; see your ML innovations directly impact how global financial markets operate
Access to cutting-edge ML infrastructure and research – Work with the latest LLMs, fine-tune foundation models, leverage enterprise-scale GPU clusters, experiment with emerging frameworks before they're mainstream, and collaborate with academic ML researchers; substantial conference and training budgets to stay at the forefront of AI innovation
Toronto as Fitch's AI center of excellence – Join our strategic investment in Toronto—one of the world's premier AI research hubs—where you'll connect with Vector Institute researchers, attend cutting-edge ML meetups, and be part of the ecosystem that's defining the future of applied AI
Shape ML governance and standards for an organization – Establish the ML engineering practices, model governance frameworks, and AI integration patterns that will guide Fitch's AI transformation; your architectural decisions will influence how a global financial services leader approaches intelligent systems
Real production impact with sophisticated ML challenges – Build ML systems that analysts and financial professionals actually use daily; solve hard problems at the intersection of NLP, document intelligence, reasoning systems, and production-scale deployment; measure your impact in both model performance and business outcomes
Accelerated career trajectory in AI leadership – High visibility to C-suite executives making billion-dollar strategic decisions; clear advancement paths to Principal ML Architect or AI Research Lead roles; opportunity to establish yourself as a recognized voice in financial AI and earn a reputation that opens doors across the industry

We'll Count On You To

Build transformative ML systems from the ground up – Design and architect net-new generative AI solutions, agentic workflows, and intelligent platforms using advanced ML frameworks (PyTorch, etc.), large language models, and emerging AI technologies that fundamentally change how analysts work and how Fitch operates
Drive breakthrough AI innovation and experimentation boldly – Lead exploration of generative AI, multi-agent systems, RAG architectures, model fine-tuning, prompt engineering, and other emerging ML technologies; create cutting-edge proofs-of-concept; evaluate what's transformative versus what's hype; and turn research into production-quality AI capabilities
Define ML technical vision and architecture for the future – Shape architectural decisions for ML systems, establish ML engineering standards, drive technology and framework choices, and influence how Fitch approaches intelligent platforms and AI governance across the organization
Lead through innovation, influence, and mentorship – Mentor and coach fellow ML engineers while partnering with product squads, business stakeholders, and cross-functional teams to translate ambitious AI ideas into elegant technical solutions; foster a culture of experimentation, continuous learning, and calculated risk-taking
Champion ML excellence while moving fast – Balance innovation velocity with ML engineering best practices; implement robust CI/CD pipelines for ML systems; develop scalable APIs (FastAPI, etc.) for model deployment; solve novel technical challenges at the intersection of cutting-edge AI research and production systems; and build solutions that are both breakthrough and reliable
Drive ML governance and operational excellence – Ensure adherence to AI/ML governance guidelines, monitor SLAs for AI solutions, optimize model performance and reliability, and translate complex ML concepts for both technical and non-technical audiences across distributed teams
Shape team culture and technical direction – Help define how our AI innovation teams operate, what "good" looks like for ML engineering, and how we balance exploration with delivery; model the curiosity, boldness, and technical rigor needed to succeed in a greenfield ML innovation environment

What You Need To Have

Deep ML technical expertise – 12+ years of professional experience building production AI/ML systems, with strong proficiency in Python, ML algorithms (from classical techniques to deep learning), and modern ML frameworks; proven track record of delivering advanced generative AI and ML solutions
ML architectural mastery and greenfield experience – Demonstrated experience designing scalable ML systems from scratch; deep understanding of ML system architecture, model deployment patterns, and the ability to make bold architectural decisions for AI platforms in ambiguous environments
Advanced generative AI expertise – Extensive hands-on experience developing and integrating generative AI solutions, working with large language models, building agentic systems, implementing RAG architectures, and training/fine-tuning neural networks using frameworks like PyTorch
Bachelor's degree in Machine Learning, Computer Science, Data Science, Applied Mathematics, or related field
Production ML engineering excellence – Deep understanding of ML operations, including containerization (Docker, Kubernetes/AWS EKS), cloud platforms (AWS/Azure), workflow orchestration (Airflow), automated testing for ML systems, and API development for model deployment
Technical leadership and influence – Track record of mentoring and coaching engineers, driving ML initiatives in fast-moving environments, leading through technical excellence and influence rather than authority, and building credibility through results and vision
Innovation and experimentation mindset – Demonstrated history of exploring emerging ML technologies, building AI proofs-of-concept, learning from failures, and translating cutting-edge research into production systems; comfort with ambiguity and rapid technological change
Outstanding collaboration and communication – Ability to articulate ML technical vision to diverse audiences, work effectively with product squads and business partners, translate complex AI/ML concepts for non-technical stakeholders, and bring your whole self while remaining open to others' perspectives

What Would Make You Stand Out

Cutting-edge AI research to production experience – Track record of taking breakthrough AI capabilities from research/prototype to production-scale deployment; experience supporting seamless transitions from experimentation to enterprise-grade ML systems with real users
ML thought leadership and technical strategy – History of establishing technical direction for ML initiatives, contributing to open-source ML projects, speaking at AI/ML conferences, publishing research, or writing about practical applications of emerging AI technologies
Multi-agent and agentic systems expertise – Hands-on experience building multi-agent systems, agentic workflows, tool-using AI systems, or complex AI orchestration platforms that go beyond simple LLM integrations
Advanced cloud-native ML infrastructure – Deep expertise building sophisticated ML infrastructure, MLOps pipelines, model serving platforms, and cloud-native AI systems at scale; experience optimizing cost and performance of production LLM deployments
Financial services or analytical domain knowledge – Understanding of analytical workflows, credit analysis processes, regulatory requirements, financial data products, or how ML enables better financial decision-making; familiarity with credit ratings agencies is a significant advantage
Startup or innovation team experience – History of building greenfield ML products, working in fast-paced AI innovation environments, or being part of 0-to-1 ML initiatives within larger organizations where you shaped technical direction
Toronto AI/ML community connection – Active participation in Toronto's AI/ML research or engineering communities, connections to academic ML research groups, or strong interest in being part of Toronto's world-class AI ecosystem

If you're ready to build transformative ML systems with organizational backing, talented colleagues, and the resources to succeed—this is the moment to join us.

Why Fitch?

At Fitch Group, the combined power of our global perspectives is what differentiates us. Our global network of colleagues comes together to accomplish things greater than they ever could alone.

Every team member is essential to our business, and each perspective is critical to our success. We embrace a diverse culture that encourages a free exchange of ideas, guaranteeing your voice will be heard and your work will have an impact, regardless of seniority.

We are building incredible things at Fitch and we invite you to join us on our journey.

About Fitch Group

Fitch Group is a global leader in financial information services with operations in more than 30 countries. Wholly owned by the Hearst Corporation, we are comprised of three main businesses: Fitch Ratings | Fitch Solutions | Fitch Learning.

For more information please visit our websites: www.fitchratings.com | www.fitchsolutions.com | www.fitchlearning.com
